The Midshipmen ended the three-game skid with a 34-26 win over the Tulsa Golden Hurricane, but they returned to the loss column after back-to-back defeats to the UTSA Roadrunners (38-34) and the North Texas Mean Green (49-39). Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Notre Dame and Navy share a long history of playing against each other in football. The former boasts 84 wins over Navy’s 13 victories while they drew once. Notre Dame took the most recent win back in November 2025, winning the game 49-10. Notre Dame has won eight consecutive games over Navy. Fighting Irish are 5-0 ATS in their last 5 vs. AC. Over is 5-0 in Fighting Irish last 5 games following a straight up loss. Over is 4-0 in Fighting Irish last 4 neutral site games as an underdog. Over is 4-0 in Fighting Irish last 4 vs. a team with a losing record. Keys to Notre Dame vs. Navy football matchup The Notre Dame Fighting Irish possess one of the best offenses in the country, shining as a fierce squad that has national championship aspirations. They rank fifth in the country in scoring offense with 41.1 points per game, 43rd in rushing offense with 183.4 yards per game and 55th in passing offense with 261.7 yards per game. CJ Carr has been productive with his playmaking, completing 129 out of 193 passes for 1,639 yards and 16 touchdowns and one interception. Jonaz Walton shines in the run game with 57 carries for 426 yards and three touchdowns, while Nolan James Jr. collected up to 81 rushes for 412 yards and six touchdowns. Jordan Faison leads the receiving corps with 34 catches for 451 yards and four touchdowns. Micah Gilbert comes next with 22 receptions for 409 yards, while Jaden Greathouse had 19 catches for 263 yards and two touchdowns. Notre Dame also shines as a strong squad on the defensive side of the ball. They rank fourth in scoring defense with 13.4 points per game, first in yards allowed with 235 yards per game, 13th in passing defense with 167.7 yards per game, and third in rushing defense with 67.3 yards per game. Drayk Bowen leads the unit with 38 tackles, two pass deflections and a fumble recovery. Bryce Young and Boubacar Traore stand out as quality pass rushers with 6.5 combined sacks, while Luke Talich is active in the secondary with 26 tackles, two interceptions and a pass deflection. The Navy Midshipmen do have bright spots amid their struggling form six games into the season. They boast the third-best rushing offense with 307.7 yards per game, while ranking 64th in scoring offense with 29.7 points per game, and 258th in passing offense with 119.4 yards per contest. Jackson Gutierrez plays a crucial role to Navy’s chances of winning games, being dominant with his rushing skills in the triple option. He has thrown for 692 yards and seven touchdowns and one interception, while rushing 150 times for 869 yards and 12 touchdowns. Michael Barrow has assisted him with 81 rushes for 442 yards and a touchdown whenever he gets touches to the ball in the offense. Jordan Collins leads receivers with six catches for 212 yards and three touchdowns, while Truman Brasfield has four receptions for 174 yards and two touchdowns. Navy has been severely vulnerable on the defensive side of the ball this year, significantly regressing from their great form throughout the 2025 season. They rank in the bottom half of the country in scoring defense with 29.1 points allowed per game. Coleman Cauley has shined with his defensive skillset as a linebacker, racking up 58 tackles and two sacks. MarcAnthony Parker follows suit with 49 tackles and four sacks, while Aiden Lyczek put together 36 tackles, 3.5 sacks and two pass deflections. Meanwhile, Giuseppe Sessi has 42 tackles, one pass deflection and an interception in the secondary. Notre Dame vs. Navy Prediction and Pick This matchup between Notre Dame and Navy stands out as an intriguing matchup. Navy is experiencing a brutal campaign on the defensive side of the ball, making this game a challenging one for the Midshipmen to deal with. They haven’t beaten the Fighting Irish in a game since 2009, a streak that will likely keep going give Notre Dame’s elite talents on both sides of the ball. Notre Dame gets the win in this one and covers, while the over also hits. Final Notre Dame vs. Navy Prediction and Pick: Notre Dame -30 (-112) and over 56.5 (-105) Related: Miami vs. North Carolina prediction, odds, pick for college football Week 9 Related: NFL picks, predictions, odds for Week 8: NFL trades make their marks

item.title: Premier League stability and European dreams: Ashton on his Ipswich plan
item.description: Mark Ashton, Ipswich Town's chairman and chief executive, has stated the club's ambition to stabilise in the Premier League and aim for Europe, among a range of topics discussed in an interview with BBC Radio Suffolk. Since taking the role in 2021, Ashton has presided over a period of exceptional success on and off the pitch, including Town twice being promoted to the top flight. In a feature interview, available on BBC Sounds , he discussed the club's transfer strategy, the desire of its investors and their shared vision for the future. Moving on from McKenna The Tractor Boys earned their third promotion in five seasons in May, sealing an immediate return to the top flight after relegation in 2024-25 . Their initial return to the Premier League came off the back of consecutive promotions from League One and the Championship, after years of stagnation since the early 2000s. However, at the end of last season, Kieran McKenna - the manager who guided the club through its period of success - unexpectedly announced he would step down , and was replaced by Gary O'Neil. Gary O'Neil took over as Ipswich manager after the departure of Kieran McKenna in June [Getty Images] The Suffolk club appear to have adapted well to the change, having already picked up three wins in the league - only one fewer than they managed in the entirety of their previous season at this level. Ahead of Saturday's trip to fellow promoted side Hull City, they sit 12th in the table. "It's been a little bit of a whirlwind," said Ashton. "He [O'Neil] has come in really calmly, very focused, strong-minded on what he wants to do, and has showed real leadership by my side on how we've stepped through all those challenges. "Without that calm leadership I don't think you get the points on the board." Are Ipswich better equipped for Premier League this time? Ashton has also got an office at the training ground "so we can work closely but make sure he has enough space to do his job". item.content:encoded: Mark Ashton, Ipswich Town's chairman and chief executive, has stated the club's ambition to stabilise in the Premier League and aim for Europe, among a range of topics discussed in an interview with BBC Radio Suffolk. Since taking the role in 2021, Ashton has presided over a period of exceptional success on and off the pitch, including Town twice being promoted to the top flight. In a feature interview, available on BBC Sounds , he discussed the club's transfer strategy, the desire of its investors and their shared vision for the future. Moving on from McKenna The Tractor Boys earned their third promotion in five seasons in May, sealing an immediate return to the top flight after relegation in 2024-25 . Their initial return to the Premier League came off the back of consecutive promotions from League One and the Championship, after years of stagnation since the early 2000s. However, at the end of last season, Kieran McKenna - the manager who guided the club through its period of success - unexpectedly announced he would step down , and was replaced by Gary O'Neil. Gary O'Neil took over as Ipswich manager after the departure of Kieran McKenna in June [Getty Images] The Suffolk club appear to have adapted well to the change, having already picked up three wins in the league - only one fewer than they managed in the entirety of their previous season at this level. Ahead of Saturday's trip to fellow promoted side Hull City, they sit 12th in the table. "It's been a little bit of a whirlwind," said Ashton. "He [O'Neil] has come in really calmly, very focused, strong-minded on what he wants to do, and has showed real leadership by my side on how we've stepped through all those challenges. "Without that calm leadership I don't think you get the points on the board." Are Ipswich better equipped for Premier League this time? Legend of the club - but McKenna leaves promoted Ipswich Ashton said O'Neil and McKenna shared "similarities", adding that O'Neil was a "great communicator" and they talked every day. Ashton has also got an office at the training ground "so we can work closely but make sure he has enough space to do his job". Not looking to stand still Ashton has been the club's chief executive since 2021 [John Fairhall/BBC] Throughout a 22-minute conversation, Ashton hammered home one point more than any other - the intention to restore Ipswich's glory days. The club became English champions for the first and only time in 1961-62, and famously won the Uefa Cup in 1981. Changes to Ipswich's ownership were made last year, with several investors coming on board , and Ashton said they were proving a driving force behind the scenes. "The investors are committed, they push hard, [and] no harder did they push on anything than they have done in the transfer window," said Ashton. "They were brutal with me on how hard they wanted me to keep the foot on the gas, and I think that related into not just the quantum of players that we brought in for both men's and women's teams, but quality, and I think both teams are bearing the fruits of that." Ipswich Town earned an immediate return to the Premier League after relegation in 2024-25 [Shutterstock] When Ipswich's men last went up to the Premier League in 2024, 10 of their 12 summer signings were British or Irish players acquired from other English sides. This time, the Blues have cast their net far wider, with Emersonn the first Brazilian to join the club, Sasa Lukic the first Serbian and Daizen Maeda their first Japanese player. "I think supporters should be really excited," Ashton added. "I still don't believe there are many, if any, clubs in the world that have had a growth period of success like we have had in the last five years, but we're not finished yet." Championship all-stars to global gamble - will Ipswich's approach work? European ambitions While many supporters will see success as securing Premier League status by means of a 17th place finish, Ashton did not shy away from sharing a vision for a return to European football for the first time since their 2002-03 Uefa Cup campaign. There is growing precedent, with the likes of Bournemouth, Brighton and Sunderland enjoying European competition this season, while clubs like Chelsea and Tottenham go without. He said: "I have one goal and that's to make this football club the best it can be. "I want it sustainably in the Premier League, I want it knocking on European football, I want it playing European football." Ashton said: "I want people to look at this football club and say actually, yeah, Sir Bobby [Robson] would have been proud of this, Sir Alf [Ramsey] would have been proud of this, because not only have they achieved success, but you know what - they've done it in a way that befits this club and its town, its county and its people." Portman Road plans Ashton said plans were being prepared to develop Portman Road and land surrounding it [Shaun Whitmore/BBC] Ashton confirmed there are plans to develop Portman Road and the area around it but said there is no set timeframe. "There's a lot of work to do," said Ashton. "There will be plans coming out over coming months for facility development, land around the stadium, how we want to take the whole Portman Road estate forward for many years to come. "There's a lot of work going on behind the scenes in regards to that and it's one to watch for the supporters." 'No time for regrets' For all of Town's successes, there have also been testing moments. Earlier this year, Ashton was forced to "unreservedly apologise" for the handling of Nigel Farage's visit to the club's Portman Road stadium. The Reform UK leader was photographed and filmed during a visit, posing with personalised shirts and pretending to sign a contract. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage visited the club's dressing room and posed for photos [Reform UK] Ashton said: "We make mistakes every single day. We don't get up every morning thinking, how are we going to make mistakes? "We get up every day trying to drive the football club forward. "There are things we would have always done differently... but there's no time for regrets. We've got to keep going and we've got to keep going quickly to drive this football club back to where it needs to be." 'Women's team destined for WSL' The goals of the men's team are clear - but Ashton said so to were its plans for the future of the women's team. He shared an unwavering belief that Ipswich Town Women, currently competing in the second tier, are on a certain path to the Women's Super League. Ipswich on 'inevitable' path to WSL - Boswell "I'm convinced of that," said Ashton. "We're building infrastructure, we're building staff, we're building quality players, we're building recruitment, we're building investment into the women's team now. "We have to build every area of this football club, both on and off the pitch, men's and women's - and I just think the future for this football club is extremely bright, but we have to build it as one. "You can't just build part of it and ignore another part, we're not going to do that." Ipswich Town Women were in the fourth tier as recently as 2021, but are now targeting a place in the Women's Super League [Shutterstock] Latest Ipswich Town news, analysis and fan views Ask about Ipswich Town - what do you want to know? item.title: Braves predicted to sign $25M ex-Yankees high-impact arm to create elite duo with Chris Sale
item.description: Braves predicted to sign $25M ex-Yankees high-impact arm to create elite duo with Chris Sale originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Braves made the postseason in 2026 after completely missing out in 2025 due to injuries and other unfortunate circumstances. Now, this offseason will be crucial as they look to strengthen their starting rotation. The biggest positive is knowing that Chris Sale will be back. However, the Braves are going to have to find reliable arms to fill out the rotation behind him. “The Atlanta Braves enter another offseason trying to solve the same puzzle: how to enhance their starting rotation. In 2026, they hoped Spencer Strider, Spencer Schwellenbach and Hurston Waldrep were the cavalry needed to solve the issues. But all three dealt with injuries and can’t be counted on to pitch in 2027,” The Athletic’s Jesus Cano wrote. A potential target just became available. Former New York Yankees and San Diego Padres starter Michael King is now a free agent. “Right-handed starter Michael King has declined the player option on his contract with the Padres to become a free agent, sources told MLB.com on Thursday. The club has not confirmed the news on King, who will now become one of the top arms on the market entering his age-32 season,” MLB.com’s AJ Cassavell wrote. With this development, Atlanta is expected to make some sort of push. Sports Illustrated’s Harrison Smajovits believes the Braves should sign King. “His 2026 season will only fortify the reasoning. He did two things that no Braves starting pitcher can claim last season. He made 32 starts and clocked over 180 innings pitched. He posted a 3.21 ERA and a 1.17 WHIP despite only posting 156 strikeouts in that time. He achieved this by reducing hard contact (just 32.7%, according to Baseball Savant) and having a solid groundball rate,” Smajovits wrote. “Here is where the reality check comes in. You can scream that he’s a fit until you’re red in the face, but they actually have to sign a starting pitcher. It’s not a Michael King issue. It’s starting pitching in general.” This would be a great pickup for Atlanta, as King has established himself as a frontline starter in the league. The Braves are in major need of a reliable arm behind Sale who can provide stability in the rotation. King made $25 million with the Padres this season before declining the remainder of his contract. Atlanta will likely have to offer a significant amount of money, but adding a dependable starter like King could be worth the investment. item.title: Some called him warlord, but he was liberator, pan-Africanist – Yormie Johnson’s widow
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Speaking about Liberia’s democratic evolution without mentioning the late Prince Yormie Johnson, better known as PYJ, would be a disservice to history. Although Johnson died on November 28, 2024, at the age of 72, he transitioned from being an officer in the Armed Forces of Liberia to becoming a democrat, senator and two-time presidential candidate. Hailing from Nimba County, the second-most populous county in Liberia, Johnson wielded considerable influence over the county’s politics, operating as a key kingmaker and political deal-broker. His support was instrumental in the emergence of presidents. His political protégé is the current Vice President of Liberia, Jeremiah Kpan Koung Sr. In this exclusive interview, the late PYJ’s widow, Mrs Amira Johnson, during a recent visit to Nigeria, shares insights into life without her husband, and struggles for the liberation of his people, describing him as a pan-Africanist. She also calls on African leaders to remain united in the interest of the continent. Excerpts: How has your experience been so far, and what has impressed you most about the country since your arrival? Well, Nigeria is like a second home to me and my family. If you could recall, my husband and I settled here briefly during the time of the crisis in Liberia. My husband was moved here by the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, and we stayed here and nurtured our children for 14 years. When the political atmosphere became stable, we had to go back and my husband contested to be a senator. So, my experience here has been so wonderful. Before now, I had come, but since my husband passed, this is my first time coming. Also, I came to SCOAN, which is my major reason for coming. I came to meet with the woman of God, Pastor Mrs TB Joshua. She and the late prophet TB Joshua had been our spiritual parents before my husband passed. While we lived in Nigeria for 14 years, that was where we used to fellowship and we went back to Liberia where we used to come from time to time. But since the prophet passed away and my husband passed on, this is my first experience. It has been wonderful. She received me warmly at the church. She hosted me. She is like a family. She welcomed me and we spent quality time visiting the mountains, doing spiritual work, praying for Liberia, praying for myself, my family and for peace and stability in the world in general. Prophet TB Joshua died five years ago. Given that you had not visited SCOAN since his passing, did you notice any change about the church? I must admit, I was quite impressed with the church. When the political atmosphere became stable, we had to go back and my husband contested to be a senator. So, my experience here has been so wonderful. Before now, I had come, but since my husband passed, this is my first time coming. Also, I came to SCOAN, which is my major reason for coming. I came to meet with the woman of God, Pastor Mrs TB Joshua. She and the late prophet TB Joshua had been our spiritual parents before my husband passed. While we lived in Nigeria for 14 years, that was where we used to fellowship and we went back to Liberia where we used to come from time to time. But since the prophet passed away and my husband passed on, this is my first experience. It has been wonderful. She received me warmly at the church. She hosted me. She is like a family. She welcomed me and we spent quality time visiting the mountains, doing spiritual work, praying for Liberia, praying for myself, my family and for peace and stability in the world in general. Prophet TB Joshua died five years ago. Given that you had not visited SCOAN since his passing, did you notice any change about the church? I must admit, I was quite impressed with the church. Nothing has changed. Pastor Mrs Evelyn Joshua, I must give it to her. In Liberia, we say she is a double person. She is two. We call them in my tradition, man-woman. She is a strong woman. What a woman. She is holding the church together. As a guest, I lodged in the church. The food, the workers, everything is in the same standard. Nothing has dropped beneath the standard they maintained when the prophet was alive. So, the organisation is top-notch. I want to give it to her. God is really using her. The auditorium was filled to capacity, just like when the man of God, Prophet TB Joshua was there. It was quite impressive. They are still the same, just like Prophet TB Joshua used to. It was quite impressive. Liberia and Nigeria share historical and cultural connections. As a Liberian visiting Nigeria once again, what similarities have you noticed between the two countries, particularly in their cultures, traditions and lifestyles? As I mentioned in my previous response, Nigeria is like a home to me. I am familiar with most of the Nigerian culture because I lived here with my late husband and children for 14 years. Nigerians are very welcoming people; we share that in common. They are very hospitable. They know how to host strangers. They are kind and generous. Nigerians are business minded. They are driven people. They go after what they want. So, we share that in common. Liberians too are kind people, very welcoming. If you meet Liberians, they are easy to deal with. So, Nigerians are like that. That is why they call them the giant of Africa, our big brother. Even though Liberia, we had our independence in 1847, Nigeria had its independence in 1960. But we as Liberians, we always look at them as our big brother in this sub-region. You were married to the late Senator Yormie Johnson, a prominent figure in Liberian politics. What are some of your fondest personal memories of him beyond his public life and political career? My late husband was known as a strong man, a very strong man. However, what many people do not know is that he had a very soft side. He was a family-oriented person. If he picked you as his person, he wanted the best for you. Sometimes, he might be difficult to access because he was always cautious However, once he took you into his corner, he could turn the world around for you. As his wife, I knew this. And for our children and everybody that came his way, he wanted the best for them. He was a friend to have in your corner. If he was for you, you would know. If he was not for you, you would also know. He was not a deceitful person. If Prince Johnson was upset with you, you would know he was. Those are some of the fondest memories. And then, for the fact that he was my husband for many years, my husband of my youth, I grew up with him. He was not just my husband, he was like a father figure to me, my children, my family and friends. I appreciate it most and I miss it to this day. Would you describe your visit to SCOAN as a way of revisiting some of the places you once visited with him? Of course I would say that, because when you are troubled as a person, you go to familiar grounds. I have had some personal issues, even in Liberia I want peace and stability, I want progress for the governance. I want harmony in my family, my children and extended family. I want the political children to be united. So, in this situation, you go to familiar grounds. I do not want division among our people. That is why coming to Nigeria feels like going down memory lane. It brings so much memory. For instance, at the time when I was alone in my room, I did not go upstairs to the suite I stayed with my husband the last time I was at the Synagogue, but I knew it was right on top of me. So, it kind of gave me those memories. And then, the last time I was in the Synagogue Church, the man of God, Prophet TB Joshua, was alive. I see his pictures all around. It still gives me that memory. It felt like his presence is still there and I know it also made me feel that even though my husband is gone, those good memories remain with me and push me on. Losing a loved one is never easy, particularly someone who played such a significant role in public life. How have you and your family been coping since his passing? Like every family, there will be disagreements here and there. Things have been tough. The void is not an easy one to fill, but we are coping and we believe that by the grace of God, spiritual guardians, things will be okay. Looking back at your husband’s life and public service, what aspects of his legacy would you particularly like future generations of Liberians to remember? My husband was a liberator of his people, of Nimba County. He is a hero in his county. Many people misjudge him. Some people call him a warlord, but for those of us and his people that know him, we know that he liberated his people. That was why he became like a hero, that his people favoured throughout his lifetime, even in his death, he is still being favoured. One of his legacies is building schools. We have junior secondary school, high school, we call it high school in Liberia. We have a church, and we have a polytechnic. Those are the legacies he left. Although it is difficult to manage, I’m hoping that we will be able to manage it and carry on his legacy. Perhaps we might do othe

item.title: Osinbajo, CJN, AGF to storm Abia for NBA-SPIDEL conference
item.description: Over 2,000 delegates expected as Otti hosts legal luminaries By Steve Oko Former Vice-President Yemi Osinbajo; the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun; and the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF), Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, are expected to storm Abia State for the 2026 Nigerian Bar Association Section on Public Interest and Development Law (NBA-SPIDEL) Annual Conference. The conference, scheduled for November 9–13 at the International Conference Centre, Umuahia, is expected to attract over 2,000 participants, including judges, lawyers, policymakers, civil society organisations, academics and development partners. The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Sir Ikechukwu Uwanna, disclosed this during a press conference at the Ministry of Justice, Umuahia, assuring participants of the state government’s commitment to a successful hosting. Uwanna said Governor Alex Otti would declare the conference open, adding that the gathering would offer participants an opportunity to assess firsthand the transformation taking place in Abia’s justice and correctional sectors. He urged NBA-SPIDEL to ensure that the conference produced practical recommendations capable of strengthening the justice system and improving citizens’ welfare, rather than ending with mere intellectual discussions. The Solicitor-General and Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Justice, Sir Paul Ogubunka, and NBA-SPIDEL Chairperson, Prof. Uju Agomoh, said the conference would provide a platform for legal practitioners and other stakeholders to promote justice, strengthen democratic institutions, protect fundamental rights and advance development through the rule of law. They noted that the gathering would facilitate critical discussions on justice delivery, democratic governance and institutional development. The Chairman of the Central Planning Committee, Sir Ejike Ezenwa, SAN; the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Legal Matters, Mrs Nkolika Ubani; and the Media and Publicity Subcommittee Chairman, Mr Obiefule Chikezie, said the conference would feature pre-conference engagements, professional development sessions and technical sessions. They commended the Otti administration for its strides in the justice sector and expressed optimism that the conference would further strengthen justice delivery and the rule of law in the state. The post Osinbajo, CJN, AGF to storm Abia for NBA-SPIDEL conference appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ballon d'Or 2026 voting breakdown: Harry Kane edges out Kylian Mbappe in incredibly tight race as full scores revealed
item.description: FBL-AWARD-BALLON D'OR-2026 - AFP Harry Kane has officially ended England's long wait for a Ballon d'Or winner, but the full voting breakdown reveals just how close the Bayern Munich striker came to missing out. The former Tottenham talisman secured the prestigious Golden Ball in London, edging out his nearest rival, Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe, in a nail-biting finish. A historic and narrow triumph Kane secured the Ballon d'Or by a razor-thin margin of just 28 points. The Bayern Munich striker claimed the coveted award for the first time on Monday, becoming the first English male player to win the prize since Michael Owen in 2001. The glitzy ceremony took place in Kane’s hometown of London, capping off a remarkable year for the Three Lions captain. The final tally highlights a fiercely competitive three-way race. Kane amassed 1,055 points, narrowly defeating Mbappe, who finished a close second with 1,027 points. Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal took third place, trailing significantly with 881 points despite a World Cup-winning campaign with Spain. A tense race to the finish line The polling process was filled with behind-the-scenes drama. France Football editor Vincent Garcia confirmed that the voting window was volatile, with the lead changing hands as the deadline approached . "I was watching the results in real time during the month of the vote," Garcia revealed. "Kylian Mbappe led the race for a long time, but Harry Kane came back into contention, and in the end, it was decided by a very, very small number of points." Following his landmark victory, Kane acknowledged the stiff competition he faced. "Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was really tough this year," he said during his acceptance speech. "Congratulations to all the winners, all the nominees tonight – an impressive showing of what determination and hard work can really achieve, so well done." A year of contrasting fortunes Mbappe’s second-place finish marks his highest-ever Ballon d'Or ranking, surpassing his third-place standing in 2018. The Real Madrid forward dominated scoring charts across La Liga, the Champions League, and the World Cup, yet remains without the Golden Ball. His lack of major club silverware last season likely proved decisive in the final vote. Conversely, Kane’s transition to Germany has been a resounding success. The striker spearheaded Bayern Munich to a domestic league and cup double, cementing their dominance in the Bundesliga. Furthermore, Kane enjoyed crucial head-to-head victories over Mbappe on the biggest stages, notably defeating Real Madrid in the Champions League to reach the semi-finals, and helping England overcome France in the World Cup third-place play-off. item.description: Image credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Cavs’ fatal flaw that will doom 2027 NBA championship chances appeared first on ClutchPoints . There is always great urgency for the Cleveland Cavaliers to finally get their breakthrough and win the NBA championship after years of being in the running. Their trade for James Harden back in February certainly put them on more of a timer as far as their contending dreams go, and they went for it even further this offseason by addressing a longstanding roster issue they’ve had in the Donovan Mitchell era by trading for a l egitimate wing player in Peyton Watson . The Cavs at least made some forward progress last season, as they made it to the Conference Finals for the first time in the Mitchell era. This was also Mitchell’s first Conference Finals appearance, individually-speaking. So it’s not like their contending dreams are dead in the water. They did get swept by the eventual champion New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference Finals, but they were competitive for stretches and may have made it a closer series had they not choked away Game 1 . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) But at the end of the day, this certain reality of how this Cavs roster is built makes it so that getting over the hump becomes very difficult and would require a lot of things to go in their favor. This is the fatal flaw that will doom the Cavs’ 2027 NBA championship chances. Overreliance on superstar backcourt could doom Cavs David Dermer-Imagn Images With Watson now on board , the Cavs have scarcely any weaknesses. They have the personnel to shapeshift depending on the opposition. Watson can contain opposing bigger forwards and provide excellent weak side help. Mario Hezonja could provide more length and range on the defensive end, and he could make opponents pay for putting smaller defenders on him. Putting Evan Mobley at the five is the solution for when they come up against speedier and smaller teams. With Jarrett Allen still on the team, the Cavs have the size as well to compete against bigger contending teams, as they can muck it up on the interior with the best of them. item.content:encoded: Image credit: David Richard-Imagn Images Cavs’ fatal flaw that will doom 2027 NBA championship chances appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There is always great urgency for the Cleveland Cavaliers to finally get their breakthrough and win the NBA championship after years of being in the running. Their trade for James Harden back in February certainly put them on more of a timer as far as their contending dreams go, and they went for it even further this offseason by addressing a longstanding roster issue they’ve had in the Donovan Mitchell era by trading for a l egitimate wing player in Peyton Watson . The Cavs at least made some forward progress last season, as they made it to the Conference Finals for the first time in the Mitchell era. This was also Mitchell’s first Conference Finals appearance, individually-speaking. So it’s not like their contending dreams are dead in the water. They did get swept by the eventual champion New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference Finals, but they were competitive for stretches and may have made it a closer series had they not choked away Game 1 . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) But at the end of the day, this certain reality of how this Cavs roster is built makes it so that getting over the hump becomes very difficult and would require a lot of things to go in their favor. This is the fatal flaw that will doom the Cavs’ 2027 NBA championship chances. Overreliance on superstar backcourt could doom Cavs David Dermer-Imagn Images With Watson now on board , the Cavs have scarcely any weaknesses. They have the personnel to shapeshift depending on the opposition. Watson can contain opposing bigger forwards and provide excellent weak side help. Mario Hezonja could provide more length and range on the defensive end, and he could make opponents pay for putting smaller defenders on him. Putting Evan Mobley at the five is the solution for when they come up against speedier and smaller teams. With Jarrett Allen still on the team, the Cavs have the size as well to compete against bigger contending teams, as they can muck it up on the interior with the best of them. Without him, they may have gotten eliminated at the hands of the Detroit Pistons in the 2026 NBA playoffs. They could even deploy Sam Merrill to chase opposing guards around screens and hound them for 94 feet, and Merrill provides the kind of shooting threat that the Cavs need after losing Max Strus. Suffice to say, depth is not the Cavs’ issue, and once again, they have come up with a solution to their questionable personnel at the three over these past few seasons. But a playoff team can only go as far as their best players can take them. Can Mitchell and Harden actually pull it off come postseason time? That is a valid question to ask. But a lot of the Cavs’ offense revolves around their superstar backcourt and whether they could fill the scoring column enough. When the going gets rough, the Cavs need to be able to rely on Mitchell and Harden to show up every single night the way Jalen Brunson did for the Knicks in their run to the title last season. And thus far, there is evidence that a team with Mitchell as its best player can only go so far. It seems like the Cavs’ star shooting guard, despite filling up the stat sheet, freezes up when the going gets rough, and that makes Cleveland susceptible to losing control of games in the fourth quarter. For instance, in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals against the Knicks, Mitchell missed all three of his shot attempts and turned the ball over once in the final 7:49 of regulation as the Cavs lost control of a 22-point lead. For any team with championship aspirations, they would want their best player to get touches and take them home during tough playoff games on the road. But Mitchell seemed almost content to defer to Harden instead of taking command of the situation and calming his team down. Mitchell has had difficulties fighting off his hero ball tendencies in the past, so perhaps this was why he wanted his teammates to be involved as well. But as the superstar of this team, the Cavs need him to strike just the right balance between getting his teammates involved and taking over when the team needs him to. This was what Brunson mastered throughout the 2026 NBA playoffs, and this is something Mitchell has to learn. This is especially the case now that Harden, who doesn’t have the best playoff track record, is a year older. At 37 years of age, Harden has lost a step or two. In five games thus far this season, the Cavs floor general is averaging 17.4 points and 6.2 assists per game, his worst numbers since his days on the Oklahoma City Thunder, while shooting a career-worst 36.2% from the field. Harden’s threat as a playmaker and shot-creator remains, but it’s evident as to which player should commandeer this Cavs team. Mitchell has to be able to leverage his elite scoring threat from distance and when attacking the basket to making his teammates better, and now that he’s 30 years of age, it might be difficult for a veteran to suddenly learn a new trick. It’s also becoming clear that this might just be who Mobley is on the offensive end. While he’s an All-Star-caliber player and a sensational defensive piece, the leap many expect on offense just may not come, which means that it’s Mitchell’s responsibility to drag this team over the hump like the great ones truly do. The recipe for a Cavs championship run seems to be very simple, at least on paper. Mitchell takes on more of a leadership role on the court and helps make his teammates better. Harden is more of an opportunistic scorer who sets up consistent openings for his teammates to exploit. Mobley blossoms into more of a consistent and assertive scorer, especially in the paint, taking advantage of mismatches. All of those will have to come together for a two-month stretch starting in April, or else the story for the Cavs come playoff time will be the same old. The San Antonio Spurs entered the 2026-27 campaign with only one goal in mind, and that is to avenge their five-game series loss to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals. After all, Many would argue that the Spurs should have won that championship after building double-digit leads in each of those five games. But the Spurs floundered when it mattered the most. In Game 2, Victor Wembanyama threw a pass off of Stephon Castle’s back, giving the Knicks the ball and the opportunity to take the lead. In Game 4, the Spurs blew a 29-point lead and lost in the final seconds to an OG Anunoby tip in. And then in Game 5, Jalen Brunson killed them off with a 45-point night. Nonetheless, it looks like everything is lining up for the Spurs to complete their redemption arc this season. The circumstances in Oklahoma City are rather unfortunate, but the Thunder experiencing a deluge of injury woes to a few core players , such as Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, and Cason Wallace, is a devastating blow to their title hopes. Anthony Edwards is out for two months and the Minnesota Timberwolves are scrambling. The Denver Nuggets look old and much worse than last season. item.content:encoded: Spurs’ fatal flaw that will doom 2027 NBA championship chances appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Antonio Spurs entered the 2026-27 campaign with only one goal in mind, and that is to avenge their five-game series loss to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals. After all, Many would argue that the Spurs should have won that championship after building double-digit leads in each of those five games. But the Spurs floundered when it mattered the most. In Game 2, Victor Wembanyama threw a pass off of Stephon Castle’s back, giving the Knicks the ball and the opportunity to take the lead. In Game 4, the Spurs blew a 29-point lead and lost in the final seconds to an OG Anunoby tip in. And then in Game 5, Jalen Brunson killed them off with a 45-point night. Nonetheless, it looks like everything is lining up for the Spurs to complete their redemption arc this season. The circumstances in Oklahoma City are rather unfortunate, but the Thunder experiencing a deluge of injury woes to a few core players , such as Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, and Cason Wallace, is a devastating blow to their title hopes. Anthony Edwards is out for two months and the Minnesota Timberwolves are scrambling. The Denver Nuggets look old and much worse than last season. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) However, the Spurs are going to have to overcome this fatal flaw if they were to finally wash away the sting of last season’s heartbreak. Can Victor Wembanyama develop a go-to offensive move? Credit: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images It’s a testament to the talent this Spurs team has that, in the first year of playoff contention with Wembanyama leading the way, they came oh so close to winning it all. But it’s also rather telling that the Spurs lost due to their subpar execution in the clutch, and a lot of that has to do with the fact that their offense sputters when up against adversity. What the Knicks did was put Karl-Anthony Towns on Wembanyama, had him body him up and push him away from the basket, and the Spurs star had difficulties getting to his spots. What made this not quite a viable game plan for the Thunder was that Isaiah Hartenstein’s presence made it so that Wembanyama could camp into the paint. Towns, of course, is known for his outside marksmanship and makes defensive rotations for the reigning Defensive Player of the Year that much more difficult. Wembanyama did not play very well during Game 1, Game 4, and Game 5 of the NBA Finals. He had to settle for difficult shots from the perimeter, and he had some troubles finishing near the basket as well as he didn’t have the strength to overpower Towns. During those three contests, all Spurs losses, Wemby shot 33.8% from the field, and a lot of that had to do with the fact that he doesn’t have a go-to scoring move. It was a catch-22 for Wembanyama. The Knicks would not allow him to set up shop near the basket, with Towns intentionally pushing him away from the hoop to make his life more difficult. Due to this, he had to catch the ball at the high post area, or even behind the three-point line. But his handle, despite being solid for a player his size, is not elite enough to the point where he can fashion clean looks for himself consistently. Just take a gander at some of the best scorers in the game today. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander’s handle is elite , he can get to his spots in the midrange at will, and his ability to make shots with defenders draped all over him is almost unparalleled in today’s NBA. Nikola Jokic, at his best, can just back up all the way to the rim, and destroy teams with his feathery touch. If they send double teams, he can just ping the ball to the open man. At this point, Wembanyama doesn’t quite have that go-to move in his offensive repertoire that he can resort to to get his team buckets when they need them. One possible solution is for him to bulk up, but at 7-foot-4, his center of gravity is always going to be high and players of Towns’ build are always just going to be able to make catches in the post difficult for him, so this isn’t exactly a catch-all panacea. Perhaps mastering the sky hook, which would be unstoppable at his height, or maybe even having his own version of the Dirk Nowitzki fadeaway would make him an even more unguardable superstar. Wembanyama is never going to be like Shaquille O’Neal who can overpower every defender that comes his way. Or he’s not going to be Hakeem Olajuwon, who was gifted with balletic feet. And that’s not necessarily bad. But having something in his repertoire that all but guarantees the Spurs two points would go a long way towards helping them get over the hump. Former Spurs star LaMarcus Aldridge already implored the 22-year-old Frenchman to develop his signature move, and then develop counter moves for it. It’s safe to say that Aldridge, who has 20,558 career points in the NBA by making a living off of that silky smooth turnaround jumper from midrange, knows what he’s talking about. Something to watch out for: the Spurs’ three-guard look Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Will starting Dylan Harper benefit the Spurs’ in the long run? Perhaps. Having their three guards (Harper, Castle, and De’Aaron Fox) get more and more accustomed to playing with one another should help them build the requisite chemistry to power this team to a title. But there might be some skillset incompatibility among those three that the Spurs have to watch out for. Those three appear to be at their best with the ball in their hands, and someone has to sacrifice touches whenever they all share the floor together. So far, Castle is the one who’s having to adjust the most. He is averaging a bonkers 8.2 three-point attempts per game heading into their Friday night contest against the Minnesota Timberwolves, which is up by over four attempts from his average last season. But as Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla said, many get so fixated over starting lineups when they’re just units that start games . Nonetheless, the Spurs have to be keeping a close eye on this situation, and they could always deploy a more balanced lineup by giving Julian Champagnie more minutes when the games matter the most and by utilizing Tobias Harris, who is currently still dealing with a calf strain. item.title: Injured Army veteran represents GB at golf in US
item.description: Steve Dickinson is representing Team GB for the third time [Simpson Cup] An injured Army veteran has been chosen to represent Great Britain in a golf competition against the US. The Simpson Cup is an international tournament for wounded and injured military veterans, taking place from Sunday at Shady Oaks Country Club in Texas. Steve Dickinson, 61, from Peterborough, needed a complete knee replacement for an injury he got after serving with the British Army in the first Gulf War in 1991 . He has been selected for the team for the third consecutive time and said: "Having served my country in uniform, being given the opportunity to represent Great Britain again through sport is something I am immensely proud of." The Simpson Cup has been running since 2012 and raises funds and awareness for the work of the On Course Foundation, which supports the recovery of wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans through golf events and opportunities for employment in the golf industry. The Ryder Cup-style tournament "showcases the unique position of golf as one of the few sports where players of all skills and abilities can play together on a level playing field, because of the official golf handicap system", the foundation said. Dickinson plays at Peterborough Milton Golf Club and his handicap is 11.7. He served with the Army Catering Corps between 1981 and 1995. Team GB currently leads the US by seven wins to six in the annual competition. Steve Dickinson celebrated with team members after their last win [Simpson Cup] Speaking about the work of the foundation, Dickinson said: "It helps us get back into civilian life, and the camaraderie, the friendship - it's just about us getting together. "My injury is nothing compared to these guys - some of them are limbless, mine was just playing football in the Army in Cyprus after the Gulf War. "I got injured and five years ago I had a full knee replacement and that's still ongoing and I need it replacing again. So it's never ending — the injury's always there." BBC Sport: Golf The foundation helps with any injury, he said. "It can be physical, it can be mental, but it helps everybody get together... it's such a great, great atmosphere." The tournaments are "full-on banter" with the opponents, "from the minute we get there to the minute we leave", Dickinson said. "We all take the mickey out of each other," he added. "But when we play the Americans, it's a serious competition to be fair; we are serious on the day." Do you have a story suggestion for Peterborough? Contact us below. Follow Peterborough news on BBC Sounds , Facebook , Instagram and X . item.title: Manchester City must give Vitor Reis more minutes after impressive Brighton performance
item.description: Manchester City must give Vitor Reis more minutes after impressive Brighton performance The more you see of Vitor Reis, the more impressive the young Brazilian centre-back is. Reis looms as a key component of the future of the Manchester City defence. However, watching Reis play against Brighton in Manchester City’s penalty shootout win in their fourth round Carabao Cup tie on Wednesday night there is one conclusion to draw. Enzo Maresca must find a way to get Vitor Reis more minutes. He is ready for a bigger role in the Manchester City squad. Vitor Reis impressed at the back as Manchester City saw off Brighton. Enzo Maresca used Manchester City’s fourth-round Carabao Cup tie as an opportunity to rotate his squad. The Manchester City fringe players were given an opportunity to impress. With the way the game played out, it was hard to pinpoint any one of City’s fringe players who seized that opportunity. One player was Vitor Reis. The young Brazilian defender put in a composed display at the back. In possession, Vitor Reis oozed class and composure. Playing against a Brighton side who are so aggressive with their high and energetic press, Reis didn’t look phased. According to statistics on SofaScore , Reis completed 58/63 of his passes. He was composed and unphased by Brighton’s press. That is a massive compliment to his talent. Defensively, Vitor Reis was solid. He wasn’t spectacular, but playing against a quality Brighton outfit didn’t bother him. He held his own and compared to Marc Guehi, who played alongside Reis at centre-back, Reis looked the more assured centre-back. There is a composure to Vitor Reis’ play when in possession or when he defends that is impossible to ignore. It is this trait that indicates Vitor Reis is ready for a more prominent role at Manchester City. Vitor Reis was rewarded for his efforts with a goal. In the 72nd minute, he deflected a Rayan Cherki shot into the net to make it 2-2. Whether or not Reis meant to finish is irrelevant. He scored a crucial goal and it was a fine reward for his overall display. Enzo Maresca needs to rest his centre-backs, Vitor Reis is ready to go. At this stage of the season Vitor Reis has been on the periphery of the Manchester City squad. He has started both of Manchester City’s Carabao Cup ties and come off the bench against Crystal Palace. But Reis is ready for a bigger role in this City squad. It is as simple as that. Enzo Maresca will need to rotate his defenders through Manchester City’s unrelenting schedule. You only have to look at Marc Guehi’s recent struggles to find evidence of this. Vitor Reis is ready to step up. It is now time he is trusted when the opportunity is there. He is more than good enough and has the composure to handle more responsibility. It is now time for him to be utilised when his more experienced teammates are struggling for form or fitness. Vitor Reis is the future of the Manchester City defence. That has been known for some time. However, he is ready to ste

item.title: The Signal: INEC Draws The Line, The Politicians Must Now Face The Voters
item.description: An important decision on governorship candidates, fresh pressure over the voters’ register, and a new battle for the South-East have shifted the 2027 campaign into more consequential territory. The politicians are still negotiating power. The electoral commission is beginning to determine who can contest it. For weeks, Nigeria’s political conversation has revolved around familiar questions. Who is supporting President Bola Tinubu? Can Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi agree on a common strategy? How much influence does Nyesom Wike command? Which governor will deliver which state? Then, on Friday, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) reminded everyone that there is another player in this election: the umpire. INEC announced the outcome of its review of complaints arising from the exclusion of governorship and state assembly candidates. Some politicians received welcome news. Others discovered that their appeals had failed. Among the most notable decisions, former Communications Minister Isa Pantami succeeded in his petition concerning the Gombe governorship election, although his candidacy remains subject to pending litigation. Ladi Adebutu, the PDP’s governorship candidate in Ogun State, was less fortunate. His petition was rejected. These decisions may appear to be administrative matters. They are not. They affect the choices available to voters, the calculations of political parties, and potentially the balance of power in important states. And they arrive at a moment when INEC is already facing intense scrutiny over the integrity of the voters’ register. The emerging question is no longer simply which politician has the strongest campaign organisation. It is whether Nigeria’s electoral institutions can apply the rules consistently, resolve disputes transparently and command public confidence when the votes are counted. Pantami gets a reprieve. Adebutu does not. INEC’s latest decisions offer a revealing picture of the difficulties political parties are experiencing with the Electoral Act and candidate nomination procedures. The commission received 69 petitions from 12 political parties across 26 states concerning governorship nominations. Of those, 41 succeeded, and 28 were rejected. For state assembly elections, 25 of the 61 petitions were successful, while 36 were rejected. The figures tell us something important. This is not an isolated disagreement involving one or two politicians. It is a substantial problem affecting party nominations across the country. The disputes concern membership registers, compliance with statutory deadlines, alleged multiple nominations and the wrongful inclusion or exclusion of candidates. INEC says it examined the complaints against relevant records and legal provisions. In Gombe, Pantami’s successful petition offers the PDP an opportunity to compete with a candidate whose exclusion had threatened its position in the state. But the pending court proceedings mean that the matter is not entirely settled

item.content:encoded: An important decision on governorship candidates, fresh pressure over the voters’ register, and a new battle for the South-East have shifted the 2027 campaign into more consequential territory. The politicians are still negotiating power. The electoral commission is beginning to determine who can contest it. For weeks, Nigeria’s political conversation has revolved around familiar questions. Who is supporting President Bola Tinubu? Can Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi agree on a common strategy? How much influence does Nyesom Wike command? Which governor will deliver which state? Then, on Friday, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) reminded everyone that there is another player in this election: the umpire. INEC announced the outcome of its review of complaints arising from the exclusion of governorship and state assembly candidates. Some politicians received welcome news. Others discovered that their appeals had failed. Among the most notable decisions, former Communications Minister Isa Pantami succeeded in his petition concerning the Gombe governorship election, although his candidacy remains subject to pending litigation. Ladi Adebutu, the PDP’s governorship candidate in Ogun State, was less fortunate. His petition was rejected. These decisions may appear to be administrative matters. They are not. They affect the choices available to voters, the calculations of political parties, and potentially the balance of power in important states. And they arrive at a moment when INEC is already facing intense scrutiny over the integrity of the voters’ register. The emerging question is no longer simply which politician has the strongest campaign organisation. It is whether Nigeria’s electoral institutions can apply the rules consistently, resolve disputes transparently and command public confidence when the votes are counted. Pantami gets a reprieve. Adebutu does not. INEC’s latest decisions offer a revealing picture of the difficulties political parties are experiencing with the Electoral Act and candidate nomination procedures. The commission received 69 petitions from 12 political parties across 26 states concerning governorship nominations. Of those, 41 succeeded, and 28 were rejected. For state assembly elections, 25 of the 61 petitions were successful, while 36 were rejected. The figures tell us something important. This is not an isolated disagreement involving one or two politicians. It is a substantial problem affecting party nominations across the country. The disputes concern membership registers, compliance with statutory deadlines, alleged multiple nominations and the wrongful inclusion or exclusion of candidates. INEC says it examined the complaints against relevant records and legal provisions. In Gombe, Pantami’s successful petition offers the PDP an opportunity to compete with a candidate whose exclusion had threatened its position in the state. But the pending court proceedings mean that the matter is not entirely settled. In Ogun, Adebutu’s unsuccessful appeal presents a different challenge. Unless the decision is overturned through a lawful process, the PDP faces the prospect of contesting the wider election without its preferred governorship candidate on the ballot. That could have consequences beyond the governorship race. State-level campaigns help mobilise supporters for other elections. They provide organisational networks, local leadership and political visibility. A party without a governorship candidate may find it more difficult to sustain enthusiasm among its supporters. But there is also a larger principle. Political parties cannot demand strict compliance with electoral law from INEC while treating their own statutory obligations as optional. If the law requires membership registers to be submitted within a prescribed period, parties must comply. Equally, INEC must demonstrate that it applies those requirements fairly to every party, whether ruling or opposition. The commission’s willingness to uphold some petitions and reject others is evidence of a review process. It is not, by itself, proof that every decision was correct. That judgment must rest on the law, the records and, where necessary, the courts. The lesson is simple: an election can be lost before polling day if a political party fails to get its nominations right. The Register Controversy Takes A More Troubling Turn If the candidate-list decisions were the day’s most consequential administrative development, the controversy surrounding the voters’ register may prove even more serious. On Friday, INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Lawrence Bayode, acknowledged that some registration officers had introduced irregular records into the commission’s database. Among the questionable entries were photographs suspected or identified as artificially generated, alongside other defective registration records. Bayode said the commission had identified how some irregularities entered the system, although the motives of those responsible remained unclear. This changes the nature of the discussion. Until now, much of the controversy had centred on screenshots circulating online and allegations from political actors. INEC’s acknowledgment provides a firmer basis for examining weaknesses in the registration process. But two distinctions are essential. First, the register under examination is preliminary, not final. INEC says its verification and cleanup processes are continuing ahead of certification on December 15. Second, the discovery of irregular entries does not establish that fraudulent votes have been cast, or that the irregularities were introduced to benefit any particular candidate. Those distinctions must not be lost in the political argument. Nevertheless, serious questions arise. How many questionable records have been identified? Were registration officers able to circumvent existing safeguards? How many records have been removed? What disciplinary or criminal investigations are underway? And perhaps most importantly, how will INEC demonstrate that its final register has been properly verified? Atiku Abubakar has demanded an independent forensic audit, identification of the officers involved, and disclosure of contractors handling sensitive election materials. He has also threatened legal action if the commission fails to provide the information sought. These demands are part of the opposition’s political response, but the underlying issue extends beyond party competition. Every candidate has an interest in an accurate register. So does every voter. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan declared on Friday, during a meeting with an ECOWAS pre-election delegation, that the commission has no preferred candidate or political party. He said INEC had completed nine of the 14 major milestones in its election timetable and outlined preparations involving biometric accreditation and electronic results management. Those assurances are important. But they must be accompanied by evidence of corrective action. The danger is not simply that irregular records may remain in the database. It is that uncertainty about the register could undermine public acceptance of the eventual election result. INEC has an opportunity to prevent that outcome. It should use it. Makinde Takes The Battle To Obi’s Political Stronghold While INEC faces questions about electoral administration, the presidential candidates are beginning to test one another’s geographical strengths. Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied People’s Movement, has taken his campaign to the South-East. At a town hall meeting in Enugu, Makinde urged voters to reject ethnic and religious considerations and examine the policy proposals of competing candidates. He acknowledged the region’s association with Peter Obi but insisted that voters should hear alternative political programmes. Makinde also outlined four pillars of his proposed ag

item.title: Pro Bowl Running Back Joe Mixon Breaks Silence After Failed Comeback Attempt
item.description: Joe Mixon shared his first public thoughts since his failed comeback. Getty Former Cincinnati Bengals and Houston Texans Pro Bowler Joe Mixon has offered his first public comments since his short-lived comeback attempt with the Seattle Seahawks, which fell through before truly beginning. “It’s all in God hands, never lose faith. [hands together/praying emoji],” Mixon posted on X on October 30. It’s all in God hands, never lose faith.🙏 — ⚡️Primetime!!!⚡️ (@Joe_MainMixon) October 31, 2026 Mixon shared a video teasing his new athletic sock line, but also teasing his comeback. The Seahawks bit, bringing him in for a visit and eleven making plans to sign the former 48th overall pick of the 2017 draft. However, the Seahawks had a change of heart after getting Mixon in for a look. “As it turns out, the Seahawks decided not to sign veteran running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad after he underwent a physical for the team, per league source,” ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported in a post on Threads on October 6, adding that “Mixon will remain a free agent.” Ex-Bengals, Texans RB Joe Mixon’s Football Future in Jeopardy Mixon’s foot injury has remained shrouded in mystery. He was spotted in a walking boot last offseason and is believed to have undergone a surgical procedure. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald did not provide any more clarity about the decision. “Just didn’t work out. Didn’t work out,” Macdonald told reporters on October 7. “Probably the most we should say about it with respect to the process. But those things happen, and it’s just part of the process.” Mixon, 30, has rushed for 7,428 yards and 60 touchdowns on 1,816 carries. He has another 2,448 yards and 14 TDs on 319 receptions. As it stands, his football future appears grim. “I don’t think this is some sort of mystery some are making it out to be,” Alexander posted on X on October 6, “He did NOT shoot himself. He has a rare medical condition he’s choosing to make private. He worked w/ doctors to help heal his foot. “The only surprise for me, is that it was never leaked to a national insider, which was likely per the request of his agent and Mixon.” Alexander called the Texans the “NFL’s most tight-lipped team” and said they “happily obliged.” Y’all just don’t know, what I been through this passed year & a half… Just know that’s all God🙏🥺 He will test your faith, keep trusting, stay patient, and believe in His timing. Never lose hope or give up. Your breakthrough is coming. 💯 — ⚡️Primetime!!!⚡️ (@Joe_MainMixon) October 5, 2026 Texans general manager Nick Caserio downplayed the idea of the injury being the result of Mixon acting irresponsibly. Head coach DeMeco Ryans opted to respect Mixon’s privacy during the ordeal. “It’s also possible those national reporters probably saw no benefit to leaking it,” Alexander said, highlighting how much uncertainty still remains around the situation. item.title: 1 stat that highlights Lakers’ brutal collapse vs. Warriors
item.description: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images 1 stat that highlights Lakers’ brutal collapse vs. Warriors appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers thought they were on their way to a dominant win over the Golden State after torching them in the first quarter of NBA Cup action on Friday night. Then the rest of the contest happened. Going into the game, Los Angeles boasted a 4-1 record. They have achieved expectations as one of the most exciting offensive squads in the league, seeing Doncic and Austin Reaves command an explosive attack on the court. The Lakers looked to be on that track again, torching Golden State 38-15 in the first quarter. It seemed that their dominance from the season opener against their division foe was going to see the same result happen. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) How Luka Doncic, Lakers played against Warriors The Warriors had other plans. They came alive for the rest of the game as Luka Doncic and the Lakers failed to regain control throughout the last three quarters. Golden State fired back with same score in the second quarter, matching Los Angeles’ 38-15 display from the first with a 38-15 outburst of their own. The Warriors ended up outscoring the Lakers 95-57 throughout the last 36 minutes, amazing fans with the big home win. Five players scored in double-digits for Los Angeles in the loss, including Doncic. He led the team with a stat line of 37 points, seven rebounds, five assists, two blocks, and one steal. He shot 12-of-27 from the field, including 6-of-16 from beyond the arc, and 7-of-8 from the free-throw line. Austin Reaves came next with 21 points and five assists, Walker Kessler had 10 points and 13 rebounds, while Jake LaRavia and Matisse Thybulle scored 10 points each. Los Angeles fell to a 4-2 record this season, sitting at fifth place in the Western Conference standings. They are above the Dallas Mavericks and the Minnesota Timberwolves while trailing the Portland Trail Blazers and the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Lakers will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being at home. They host the Toronto Raptors as tip-off commences on Nov. 1 at 9 p.m. ET. Related: Luka Doncic makes NBA history vs. Warriors Related: Lakers fans clown Yaxel Lendeborg after dominant Luka Doncic performance

He shot 12-of-27 from the field, including 6-of-16 from beyond the arc, and 7-of-8 from the free-throw line. Austin Reaves came next with 21 points and five assists, Walker Kessler had 10 points and 13 rebounds, while Jake LaRavia and Matisse Thybulle scored 10 points each. Los Angeles fell to a 4-2 record this season, sitting at fifth place in the Western Conference standings. They are above the Dallas Mavericks and the Minnesota Timberwolves while trailing the Portland Trail Blazers and the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Lakers will look to bounce back in their next matchup, being at home. They host the Toronto Raptors as tip-off commences on Nov. 1 at 9 p.m. ET. Related: Luka Doncic makes NBA history vs. Warriors Related: Lakers fans clown Yaxel Lendeborg after dominant Luka Doncic performance

item.title: Warriors predicted to trade for Thunder's 7-foot-1 NBA champion to replace Kristaps Porzingis
item.description: Warriors predicted to trade for Thunder's 7-foot-1 NBA champion to replace Kristaps Porzingis originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . For the Golden State Warriors , it has been an okay start to the season, but the most frustrating part of the offseason came from their inability to sign any big-name players. One of the players Golden State did sign was veteran Kristaps Porzingis. The seven-footer is known for his size, but also for his history of missing significant time due to injuries. Porzingis has not been around the team since training camp began. “That has meant an out-of-sight, out-of-mind strategy when it comes to the ongoing absence of presumed starting center Kristaps Porzingis, who was re-signed this summer despite missing 90 games over the past two seasons with three different teams. Ever since Porzingis called out of work one day prior to training camp, the front office instructed Steve Kerr to strategize and prep his team as if Porzingis was a nonfactor,” ESPN’s Anthony Slater wrote. With it being highly unlikely that Porzingis plays this season, or perhaps ever again, the Warriors are trying to find a trade partner. “Golden State has started exploring trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis, who is now seriously contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autoimmune condition termed as POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome), sources tell ESPN," ESPN's Shams Charania posted. Through the first week of the season, it has become clear that Golden State is undersized. Bleacher Report’s Dan Favale believes the Warriors could trade for Oklahoma City Thunder center Chet Holmgren. “Perhaps Aday Mara is so good so fast that the Oklahoma City Thunder end up rethinking their monster commitment to Chet Holmgren amid an expected belly flop into second-apron territory next season,” Favale wrote. Holmgren would be a great replacement for Porzingis, as he is younger and the Warriors would have control over him for the next few seasons. Holmgren also already has championship experience. Holmgren is currently on a $239 million contract with the Thunder. The Warriors are in major need of size, and acquiring Holmgren would be a significant addition. It would also benefit Steph Curry tremendously. All of this would need to happen when he recovers from his injury of course. item.title: Lakers fans clown Yaxel Lendeborg after dominant Luka Doncic performance
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Lakers fans clown Yaxel Lendeborg after dominant Luka Doncic performance appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The ongoing feud between Luka Doncic and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has increasingly resembled a dramatic rivalry. On Friday, Lendeborg had the last laugh as the Golden State Warriors secured a 112-95 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers . However, the rookie struggled to make an impact against Doncic’s outstanding performance, which quickly made him a target of criticism and trolling from Lakers fans. Lendeborg made a statement before the game by arriving at the arena dressed in a Michael Myers costume. Such a bold entrance naturally raised expectations for his performance on the court. However, Doncic stole the spotlight with his dominant display, leaving the Warriors rookie facing plenty of online mockery. “ Yaxel Lendeborg did all that to show up and drop 6 points,” one fan mocked . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Yaxel 6’9 for nothing dude plays trash against the Lakers but good against everybody else,” a fan remarked . “ Yaxel Lendeborg is currently a -22 while his team is winning by 12 points and Luka Doncic is a +11 while being down 12 points,” one user added . “NBA hypes up the Luka and Yaxel Lendeborg beef only for Yaxel to have zero shot attempts all game,” another comment read . The Lakers superstar finished with 37 points, seven rebounds and five assists in 37 minutes. He shot 12-of-27 from the field, including 6-of-16 from beyond the arc, and converted seven of his eight free-throw attempts. Doncic also recorded one steal and two blocks. Meanwhile, Lendeborg finished with six points and one rebound in 24 minutes for the Warriors. However, he did not record an assist and finished with five turnovers and six personal fouls. Despite Lendeborg’s modest contribution, the Warriors managed to come away with the victory behind another impressive performance from Stephen Curry. Golden State found itself trailing Los Angeles by as many as 25 points early in the second quarter, but the team gradually turned things around and eventually secured a 17-point win. The loss dropped the Lakers to a 4-2 record for the season, while Golden State improved to 3-3. Related: Luka Doncic makes NBA history vs. Warriors Related: 1 stat that highlights Lakers’ brutal collapse vs. Warriors

item.title: “How Many All-Pros Does Tom Brady Have?”: Rob Parker Makes Massive Claim About Lamar Jackson’s NFL Legacy By Comparing Him To 7x SB Winner
item.description: Lamar Jackson © Imagn NFL analyst Rob Parker showered praise on Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson and compared him to seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady. On The Odd Couple Show, Parker highlighted Jackson’s three First-Team All-Pro selections and compared them with Brady, who earned the same number in 23 seasons. “The best quarterback in the NFL is Lamar Jackson,” Parker said. “How many All-Pros does Tom Brady have? Tom Brady had three All-Pros. Three in 23. Lamar has three already in two-thirds less time. He already has three.” Brady also had three Second-Team All-Pro selections. The former Patriots quarterback won three MVP awards, while Jackson has won two. Parker added that Jackson was robbed of the MVP award in 2024 and claimed he had a better season than eventual winner, Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen. “He should have three MVPs,” Parker continued. “The best year he had in the National Football League didn’t give him the MVP. They gave him first-team All-Pro, but they gave Josh Allen the MVP because they felt sorry for him. It went against everything we know in the National Football League. It was terrible.” In that season, Jackson threw for 4,172 yards, 41 touchdowns and four interceptions. Meanwhile, Allen threw for 3,731 yards, 28 touchdowns, and six interceptions. In the voting , Allen received 383 points and 27 first-place votes, while Jackson finished with 362 points and 23 first-place votes. Rob Parker Excuses Lamar Jackson Of Super Bowl-Less Career While Lamar Jackson is considered one of the best quarterbacks in the league, his lack of postseason success takes some of the shine off his career. Tom Brady made 10 Super Bowl appearances and won seven championships. On the other hand, Jackson has zero Super Bowl appearances in eight seasons. However, according to Rob Parker, the Ravens quarterback has been let down by his teammates. “Zay Flowers, a fumble. Mark Andrews can’t catch a two-point conversion to tie the game in Buffalo. It’s happened over and over again,” Parker said. “Last year, to get into the playoffs and to win the division, guess what happened? Lamar drove the team down the field in Pittsburgh, and the kicker missed a field goal.” Jackson has missed three straight games due to a high ankle sprain sustained in Week 4, but is expected to return when the Ravens face the Bills on Sunday.
