item.title: WWE succession plan emerges as Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles eye new roles
item.description: Photo by MICHAEL TRAN/AFP via Getty Images WWE Hall of Famers Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles are reportedly in line for major backstage promotions as the company prepares for a significant change in its creative leadership. Bruce Prichard, WWE’s Executive Director of Creative Writing and Talent, is expected to retire after WrestleMania 43, although he could remain involved with the company as a consultant. Michaels is reportedly being lined up to replace Prichard in 2027, while Styles could take on a more hands-on role with WWE’s developmental brand, NXT. Shawn Michaels could replace Bruce Prichard as AJ Styles takes on NXT role According to reports from PWInsider , Michaels is expected to move into Prichard’s position, with preparations for the transition already expected to begin in the coming months. The former WWE champion has led NXT since 2021, when Paul ‘Triple H’ Levesque underwent a cardiac procedure. Michaels was subsequently promoted to Senior Vice President of Talent Development and Creative. His experience with developing young wrestlers makes him a natural candidate for a more prominent position within WWE’s creative structure. Michaels also shares a longstanding friendship with Triple H, which could prove valuable as the pair continue shaping the company’s future. However, his potential promotion would leave a significant opening at NXT, with AJ Styles reportedly emerging as a candidate to take on greater responsibilities. According to False Finish, WWE officials expect Styles to become more involved with the developmental brand following Michaels’ departure from the role. Styles has previously expressed a desire to help prepare the next generation of WWE superstars, particularly after stepping away from in-ring competition. Triple H discussed the former champion’s plans during an appearance on Cody Rhodes’ podcast, explaining that Styles had explored several backstage positions before identifying the area that suited him best. “He really likes is getting to these young kids, spotting talent, and trying to help fan the flames of that little spark and turn it into something more, the developmental side,” Triple H said. Styles’ interest in mentoring young wrestlers could make him a strong fit for NXT, where emerging talent is prepared for the main roster. The Phenomenal One brings plenty of experience to the role, having won both WWE and TNA World Championships and becoming one of just 22 Grand Slam champions in WWE history. Styles was also inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame during WrestleMania 42 week. With Prichard’s expected retirement approaching, WWE could soon have two familiar names taking on new responsibilities behind the scenes. item.title: Mike Brown calls out the Knicks' mediocre defense in the loss against the 76ers
item.description: Mike Brown calls out the Knicks' mediocre defense in the loss against the 76ers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In the New York Knicks ' first game in their NBA Cup defense, they unfortunately lost the game 98-93 to the Philadelphia 76ers . It was a superb performance by the 76ers ' Tyrese Maxey, but it seems they really capitalized on the Knicks ' defense. New York head coach Mike Brown was frustrated about how the Knicks looked on defense. It was a frustrating night because it was a big blow to the hopes of an NBA Cup repeat and another loss that drops them to a 2-4 record. Mike Brown laments the Knicks' troubling defense against the 76ers It is a challenging result for the Knicks because the Knicks had the chance to get back on track to a 3-3 record. Unfortunately, they suffered yet another loss to the 76ers, which gives them a 2-0 edge in the head-to-head matchup. While Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns scored over 20 points apiece, it was still quite an underwhelming performance for the Knicks. This is not what people would like to see, especially with their status as defending champions. MORE: Mike Brown's reality check from the slow start to the Knicks' season Scoring 93 points is not the optimal approach to a game but it seems that Brown had more of a problem with what transpired on defense. He was not a fan of how easy the 76ers had it at certain points in the game. "Gotta give Philadelphia credit; they won the ball game. When you watch this game, though, especially in the first half, how they got downhill so easily. They were getting in our paint left and right. It was really, really easy; we weren't in our shifts," Brown said about the Knicks' defense after the game . "To continue to have that ball dribbling into the paint, especially in the paint when they shot 5-7 from the three-point line, was not good." Brown also commented about how the Knicks are trying to hit home runs on every offensive play. It is definitely an inconsistent approach to the game across both sides of the ball, and Brown wants to fix that moving forward if they want any chances of getting back to the top of the Eastern Conference standings. item.title: Teen football photographer 'living the dream'
item.description: Tiego Greno has progressed from photographing lower league matches to Premier League games [Tiego Greno] From taking photos of grassroots football matches up to Champions League games - all by the age of 18 - Tiego Greno says he is "living the dream". The teenager from Chelmsford started taking photos of lower league football in 2023, before becoming Chelmsford City's club photographer for the 2025-26 season. Now he has started taking photos of Premier League and European matches, including Arsenal's recent away fixture against Bayern Munich. "I just want to be everywhere, every single day if it's possible," he told the BBC. Greno started work with a photography agency aged 17 which was something he says came with challenges, given his age. "Many of these stadiums don't allow anyone under 18 to work in those environments, so I had to be restricted," he told BBC Essex's James Patient. Still only 18, Greno's photography has taken him to stadiums including Real Madrid's Bernabeu [Tiego Greno] But his work began to speak for itself. Just three days after his 18th birthday, he won the sports category at the East Anglian Photography Awards, with his photo of Southend United players crestfallen as their opponents Oldham Athletic celebrated promotion back to the Football League at Wembley Stadium in June 2025. "I think that picture really summarised what can happen in the sport - you could be winning for the entire game and then in the last minute it all turns around," he said. Greno says he is grateful to his family for being able to afford his camera equipment, especially his father and fellow photographer Antonio. "Without him, probably I wouldn't be where I am right now," he said. Antonio said it was "impossible not to be proud" of his son. "For me, this journey has been… more than photography, it's been about watching my son discovering what he loves and, most importantly, having the courage to follow," he told the BBC. His son said: "I'm already living the dream. It's just keeping it really consistent and if I can do it every day, perfect." Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below. Follow Essex news on BBC Sounds , Facebook , Instagram and X . item.description: 1 trade Texans must make during 2026 NFL season bye week appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Texans have spent the first seven weeks of the 2026 NFL season discovering just how expensive weaknesses in the trenches can become. Despite boasting some really explosive offensive weapons and some of the league’s most dangerous pass rushers, Houston has repeatedly struggled to control the line of scrimmage. Their latest defeat against the New York Giants exposed a particularly alarming vulnerability. Now with the bye week here , general manager Nick Caserio must consider making an aggressive move before the trade deadline. Acquiring Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea could be that move. Defensive reset Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The Texans’ 2026 campaign to date has been an excruciating sequence of narrow misfires and emotional turbulence. Four of their five losses have come in one-score heartbreakers. Houston opened the year with an alarming four-game slide. With DeMeco Ryans taking over defensive play-calling duties, the team mounted an emphatic response by suffocating Tennessee on the road. That was before pulling off an electric transatlantic victory over Jacksonville in London. And then, the momentum screeched to a halt inside NRG Stadium with a deflating 27-21 overtime defeat to the Giants . That exposed glaring structural breakdowns at the line of scrimmage. The urgent reality is that cosmetic adjustments during the bye week simply will not suffice. Dominant interior anchor The Texans’ most pressing defensive weakness is their inability to consistently stop downhill rushing attacks. In Week 7, their defense surrendered 188 rushing yards and allowed consecutive overtime gains of 42 and 30 yards. Ryans’ defensive philosophy depends on controlling the interior and occupying blockers. Unfortunately, Houston’s defensive tackles have struggled to provide that dependable foundation. The Houston Texans have spent the first seven weeks of the 2026 NFL season discovering just how expensive weaknesses in the trenches can become. Despite boasting some really explosive offensive weapons and some of the league’s most dangerous pass rushers, Houston has repeatedly struggled to control the line of scrimmage. Their latest defeat against the New York Giants exposed a particularly alarming vulnerability. Now with the bye week here , general manager Nick Caserio must consider making an aggressive move before the trade deadline. Acquiring Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea could be that move. Defensive reset Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The Texans’ 2026 campaign to date has been an excruciating sequence of narrow misfires and emotional turbulence. Four of their five losses have come in one-score heartbreakers. Houston opened the year with an alarming four-game slide. With DeMeco Ryans taking over defensive play-calling duties, the team mounted an emphatic response by suffocating Tennessee on the road. That was before pulling off an electric transatlantic victory over Jacksonville in London. And then, the momentum screeched to a halt inside NRG Stadium with a deflating 27-21 overtime defeat to the Giants . That exposed glaring structural breakdowns at the line of scrimmage. The urgent reality is that cosmetic adjustments during the bye week simply will not suffice. Dominant interior anchor The Texans’ most pressing defensive weakness is their inability to consistently stop downhill rushing attacks. In Week 7, their defense surrendered 188 rushing yards and allowed consecutive overtime gains of 42 and 30 yards. Ryans’ defensive philosophy depends on controlling the interior and occupying blockers. Unfortunately, Houston’s defensive tackles have struggled to provide that dependable foundation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The consequences extend beyond stopping the run. When opposing offenses consistently generate manageable second and third downs, they can dictate the tempo. They can prevent Houston’s pass rushers from operating in favorable situations. Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter are considerably more dangerous when they can attack quarterbacks in obvious passing situations. They should not spend entire afternoons trying to compensate for defensive breakdowns against the run. Houston needs a legitimate space-eater who can absorb double teams and hold his ground. The Texans need someone who can prevent opposing offensive lines from establishing movement at the point of attack. That is precisely the type of player Nick Caserio should pursue. Vita Vea The ideal solution is Tampa Bay Buccaneers defensive tackle Vita Vea. At 6-foot-4 and approximately 347 pounds, Vea possesses the combination of size, strength, and mobility necessary to transform an interior defensive line. The two-time Pro Bowler has established himself as one of the NFL’s premier interior run defenders. He can use his tremendous lower-body strength to occupy multiple blockers and disrupt rushing lanes. His ability to command attention would immediately change the dynamics of Houston’s defensive front. There is, however, one significant obstacle. Vea is not an uncomplicated trade target. He requested a trade during the summer amid contract negotiations. Tampa Bay, though, subsequently agreed to a contract extension. That keeps him under contract through 2027. Buccaneers general manager Jason Licht has also made clear that the organization has no intention of casually moving him. That makes acquiring him considerably more difficult, but not necessarily impossible. Caserio should at least explore Tampa Bay’s willingness to entertain an offer. This is particularly true if Houston is prepared to surrender meaningful future draft compensation. A 2027 third-round selection could serve as an opening proposal. Of course, Vea’s new contract and importance to Tampa Bay might demand a more substantial package. Pairing Vea with Sheldon Rankins would give Houston a formidable interior combination. Vea’s ability to occupy blockers would create opportunities for Rankins to penetrate gaps. It could also allow Anderson and Hunter to attack opposing quarterbacks with fewer distractions. Changing trajectory Image Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The Texans cannot afford to waste another season of their current defensive core because of a problem that can potentially be addressed through an aggressive personnel move. At 2-5, Houston still has considerable ground to make up. Its narrow defeats. though, suggest that the team is not necessarily miles away from becoming competitive again. Improving the interior defensive line could have an immediate ripple effect. It can help the linebackers play faster and make the pass rush more effective. It can also give the defense a better chance of protecting fourth-quarter leads. Vea would not magically solve every issue on Ryans’ roster . The financial and draft-capital implications deserve careful consideration as well. Nevertheless, dominant interior defenders are difficult to find. Houston has a particularly compelling reason to prioritize one. Caserio must be willing to think aggressively rather than settle for minor adjustments. If Tampa Bay is willing to negotiate, acquiring Vea should be firmly on the Texans’ radar. The road back to contention starts in the trenches. This is one investment that could make Houston considerably more dangerous. Related: Texans’ biggest problem to fix during 2026 bye week Related: Texans’ 7-round 2027 NFL Draft according to PFF mock draft simulator during bye week

item.title: Mission Viejo defeats San Juan Hills in an Alpha League shootout
item.description: Mission Viejo High players and coaches pose for a photo after winning the Alpha League title on Friday night at San Juan Hills (Caleb Otte / For The Times) Scoring 44 points in a league championship decider is usually enough to secure victory — but not against Mission Viejo. The Diablos beat San Juan Hills 54-44 in an epic Orange County shootout to secure its third consecutive Alpha League crown, buoyed by a bevy of explosive plays. It started in the first quarter as senior running back Carson Vandermade, who returned after missing the last two games, scored two touchdowns. He finished the game with 121 yards, including a big 52-yard run down the sideline, and three touchdowns but did not return for the fourth quarter. His counterpart, senior Jack Junker, gained 132 yards, including a 28-yarder, and two touchdowns as the Diablos’ rushing attack dominated. Every time Vandermade and Junker took handoffs, there was a gift waiting. The offensive line — which has four players either committed to or with offers to Division I colleges — opened up huge running lanes. Junior center Max Davidson attributed the group’s success to a deep camaraderie and hard work. “It comes down to all the time that we put in together,” he said. “It comes down to the chemistry that we have between the five of us up front. We work together really well and that shows in all our games.” Mission Viejo High center Max Davidson is all smiles after the Diablos won the Alpha League title with a 54-44 victory over San Juan Hills on Friday night. (Caleb Otte / For The Times) Sophomore quarterback Brett Burnor also got in on the rushing action, with 30 yards and two touchdowns. He had a solid night through the air, connecting on nine of his 12 passes for 188 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Burnor had four passes that went for more than 30 yards and connected most often with senior wide receiver Luke Karby, a Duke commit who had 122 yards on five receptions and made multiple contested catches. Karby also threw a two-point conversion to Burnor, in a quick role reversal, in the second quarter. Mission Viejo coach Chad Johnson said before kickoff that the game would be decided by explosive plays, and he wanted to limit the opponent’s electric moments. “Every game, San Juan Hills has six to 10 explosive plays on offense that are 40- to 60-yard chunk plays,” he said. The Diablos allowed San Juan Hills to stay within fighting distance via those big gains that Johnson warned against. While the home team never trailed, San Juan Hills cut the score to 47-44 midway through the fourth quarter after an improbable onside kick recovery. Senior kicker Trevor Koko continued an impressive season with a looping ball that Mission Viejo wasn’t able to field, breathing life into a potential comeback. item.content:encoded: Mission Viejo High players and coaches pose for a photo after winning the Alpha League title on Friday night at San Juan Hills (Caleb Otte / For The Times) Scoring 44 points in a league championship decider is usually enough to secure victory — but not against Mission Viejo. The Diablos beat San Juan Hills 54-44 in an epic Orange County shootout to secure its third consecutive Alpha League crown, buoyed by a bevy of explosive plays. It started in the first quarter as senior running back Carson Vandermade, who returned after missing the last two games, scored two touchdowns. He finished the game with 121 yards, including a big 52-yard run down the sideline, and three touchdowns but did not return for the fourth quarter. His counterpart, senior Jack Junker, gained 132 yards, including a 28-yarder, and two touchdowns as the Diablos’ rushing attack dominated. Every time Vandermade and Junker took handoffs, there was a gift waiting. The offensive line — which has four players either committed to or with offers to Division I colleges — opened up huge running lanes. Junior center Max Davidson attributed the group’s success to a deep camaraderie and hard work. “It comes down to all the time that we put in together,” he said. “It comes down to the chemistry that we have between the five of us up front. We work together really well and that shows in all our games.” Mission Viejo High center Max Davidson is all smiles after the Diablos won the Alpha League title with a 54-44 victory over San Juan Hills on Friday night. (Caleb Otte / For The Times) Sophomore quarterback Brett Burnor also got in on the rushing action, with 30 yards and two touchdowns. He had a solid night through the air, connecting on nine of his 12 passes for 188 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Burnor had four passes that went for more than 30 yards and connected most often with senior wide receiver Luke Karby, a Duke commit who had 122 yards on five receptions and made multiple contested catches. Karby also threw a two-point conversion to Burnor, in a quick role reversal, in the second quarter. Mission Viejo coach Chad Johnson said before kickoff that the game would be decided by explosive plays, and he wanted to limit the opponent’s electric moments. “Every game, San Juan Hills has six to 10 explosive plays on offense that are 40- to 60-yard chunk plays,” he said. The Diablos allowed San Juan Hills to stay within fighting distance via those big gains that Johnson warned against. While the home team never trailed, San Juan Hills cut the score to 47-44 midway through the fourth quarter after an improbable onside kick recovery. Senior kicker Trevor Koko continued an impressive season with a looping ball that Mission Viejo wasn’t able to field, breathing life into a potential comeback. A quick touchdown drive ensued that made the final minutes extra nervy for the Diablos. Ultimately, the rushing attack killed the clock and clinched the win by grabbing one more touchdown on an 11-yarder by Junker with 40 seconds to play. San Juan Hills backup quarterback Parker Armstrong was given the reins to let the ball loose by coach Robert Frith. He completed 27 of 37 passes for 343 yards and four touchdowns with one interception. His longest of the night came on a quick dump down to senior wide receiver commit Luke Frith, a Texas State commit who took it 80 yards for a touchdown. Another long score came on a slant route to senior wide receiver Cooper Chila who broke multiple tackles to take it 57-yards to the house. Those plays summed up much of the game for the Stallions. Athletic players making big plays, and never giving up on the game. San Juan Hills lost, but it never gave up. Frith’s constant messaging to the players clearly got through. The Stallions’ coach said he always tells the team: “When that ball snaps, it is seven seconds of everything you’ve got.” The game was a high octane battle, but there will be a lot to parse through in the film room, especially for Mission Viejo. In the midst of the barnstorming action, the victors had three bad snaps on extra points and 18 penalties, including six personal foul calls. Johnson lamented what he called poor officiating after the game but also told his team that the errors needed to be cleaned up by next week’s playoff opener. Mission Viejo likely qualified for the Southern Section Division 1 playoffs with this the win, and will learn of its opponent on Sunday. San Juan Hills will finish the regular season with two losses and wait to see if it makes the Division 2 playoffs. Sign up for the L.A. Times SoCal high school sports newsletter to get scores, stories and a behind-the-scenes look at what makes prep sports so popular. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

item.title: 'Showed me a lot': Skip Bayless reacts to what Luka Doncic did after Steph Curry 'broke his ankles'
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Stephen Curry and Luka Doncic, unsurprisingly, have made the headlines following the Golden State Warriors’ 112-95 win over the Los Angeles Lakers in the NBA Cup. The Lakers started the game in tremendous fashion, leading the first quarter 38-15. At one point in the game, they were even 25 points ahead, but they ended up losing by 17 in the end. The most eye-catching moment, though, was when Curry embarrassed Doncic before scoring a three-pointer. Skip Bayless praises Luka Doncic’s reaction after Steph Curry dropped him Both Doncic and Curry are among the best players in the NBA, so seeing them go up against each other is always a treat. On Friday night, after a stunning first-quarter performance by the Slovenian, Curry turned up and helped his side win the game. At one moment, when Doncic and Curry came face to face, ‘the latter’s dribbling skills caused the Lakers star to lose his balance and fall down. Curry then calmly converted a three-pointer, making that a very memorable moment. We’re sure it will be played back over and over again. Despite that, Doncic showed immense class after the game and shook hands with all the Warriors players. That caught Skip Bayless’ eye. He tweeted: “Luka showed me a lot by congratulating the Warriors stars, especially Steph, who “broke his ankles.”” That really was great to see, and it showed what kind of a man Doncic is. He could easily have walked back into the locker room, but staying back to congratulate the opponents after a defeat and an embarrassing moment is a classy move. item.title: Pistons predicted to trade for $179M ex-Nuggets sharpshooting NBA champion to address weakness
item.description: Pistons predicted to trade for $179M ex-Nuggets sharpshooting NBA champion to address weakness originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Pistons were the best team in the Eastern Conference during the regular season last year, but they quickly realized they were still an inexperienced group when it came to the playoffs. This season, they are hungry to get back and prove they can take the next step. However, the organization explored several different ways to bring star players to the Motor City. They were prepared to offer Austin Reaves a contract and also made calls about Kevin Durant and Kawhi Leonard. “The Pistons inquired about trading for Kawhi Leonard and Kevin Durant this offseason, according to league sources, and were positioned to offer Austin Reaves a big free agent contract if the Los Angeles Lakers opened the door. None of that materialized," ESPN's Vincent Goodwill wrote. One of the biggest weaknesses from last season that could continue to hold Detroit back is its ability to shoot from beyond the three-point line. “Most notably, the Pistons are even snagging wins when they shoot poorly from beyond the arc. In an era of basketball where consistency from three-point range is preached as paramount, the Detroit Pistons are winning in their own way. Their tough defense and efficiency inside the paint has defined their identity this season," SI's Aidan Chacon wrote. Adding a shooter will undoubtedly be one of the Pistons' priorities ahead of the trade deadline. CBS Sports' Sam Quinn believes they should pursue a trade for NBA champion Michael Porter Jr. “Get ready to hear a lot about the Detroit Pistons today, folks. A team that needs offense and controls all of its own picks is always going to feature prominently in deadline speculation, and Porter is the first of many candidates who will come up for them here,” Quinn wrote. Porter would be a great addition because he offers exactly what the team needs as a shooter while also bringing NBA Finals experience. He could become an important presence in Detroit's locker room as well. Porter is currently playing on a $179 million contract with the Brooklyn Nets and is coming off a strong campaign last season. If the Pistons want to add a proven scorer, Porter would certainly be a good option. item.title: Tottenham receive MASSIVE James Maddison injury boost ahead of Crystal Palace clash
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Coventry City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham Hotspur have received a significant boost with manager Roberto De Zerbi confirming James Maddison is available to face Crystal Palace on Saturday. The England international suffered an injury scare against Chelsea, but he is now in contention to feature alongside the returning Destiny Udogie. Maddison shakes off injury scare Maddison has been cleared to play against Palace in the Premier League this Saturday. The England international sparked injury fears after being substituted early in the second half of a 2-0 victory at Chelsea . However, manager De Zerbi confirmed the playmaker has avoided a serious setback. Maddison will now be part of the matchday squad for the weekend fixture. De Zerbi confirms special player is available Maddison followed a modified training programme this week to manage his workload following the early substitution. Despite missing a couple of full sessions, De Zerbi insists the midfielder is ready to contribute. "This week he didn't work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us," De Zerbi told a press conference on Friday. The Tottenham boss must now decide whether to start the midfielder or utilise him from the bench against Palace. The coaching staff will evaluate his final fitness levels before kick-off. Managing a careful return to fitness Fitness remains a sensitive topic for Maddison after a difficult period on the sidelines. He missed the majority of last season with an ACL injury and suffered a shoulder problem during an opening-weekend defeat at Brentford. He recently marked his return to the starting XI by opening the scoring against Coventry City earlier this month. The club is now taking a cautious approach to ensure he stays fit for the remainder of the campaign. "For Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks," De Zerbi added. "So, I think it's not a problem if he loses two days, but then we have to analyse if we take the risk or not." Udogie returns to bolster the squad Maddison is not the only player returning to action for Tottenham this weekend. Full-back Udogie is also set to feature after missing the last two games with a knee injury. The dual return of Maddison and Udogie provides a massive lift for the team. De Zerbi will hope to capitalise on a strengthened starting lineup as they look to secure three vital Premier League points.

By the time New York established the urgency it needed, the margin for error had disappeared. His postgame assessment explained why a competitive finish did not make the earlier problems any easier to overlook. “Today we played like a team that was on the end of a road trip,” Towns said. “We gotta find that gear. We gotta find that energy.” That is a direct assessment from one of the Knicks’ most important players. Towns recognized the difference between how New York started and how it eventually competed. For fans expecting more, that gap deserves attention. Karl-Anthony Towns Explains Knicks’ ‘Quicksand’ Problem “I thought we did a great job in that fourth quarter of finding that gear, like you said, just kind of getting out of the quicksand,” Towns said. “To do that puts us in a position where you gotta make some magic happen, and we just didn’t have enough magic tonight.” The quicksand comparison captures the frustration. New York showed it could raise its level, but doing so late left the team needing nearly everything to break its way. A fourth-quarter push can create an opportunity without undoing the possessions that made such a push necessary. Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – OCTOBER 30: Adem Bona #30 of the Philadelphia 76ers falls on top of Karl-Anthony Towns #32 of the New York Knicks during the second half of an Emirates NBA Cup game at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) That distinction matters when evaluating this performance. The Knicks deserve credit for putting themselves back in contention. However, praising the response should not prevent an honest discussion about why they needed one. Knicks Need Urgency Before the Fourth Quarter Philadelphia ultimately won 98-93, despite 22 points and 12 rebounds from Towns. Jalen Brunson added 24 points, and New York briefly grabbed a late lead before the Sixers answered. The opportunity was there, which makes the result difficult to accept. For New York, the useful question is how to establish that fourth-quarter intensity earlier. Better urgency can show up through sharper cuts, quicker defensive reactions and more commitment to finishing possessions. Those details give a team a chance to control the game instead of constantly chasing it. Towns’ comments should resonate because they acknowledged both the encouraging response and the underlying concern. New York found another gear, but the timing left too much work unfinished. The Knicks need that energy to become their starting point, giving their talent more room to decide games before desperation enters the picture. item.title: Where to watch Ferris State vs. Davenport today: Channel, live stream, time, schedule for D2 Top 10 matchup
item.description: Where to watch Ferris State vs. Davenport today: Channel, live stream, time, schedule for D2 Top 10 matchup originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ferris State has dominated Division II football for the better part of three years, but its rivals are inching closer. The top-ranked Bulldogs (8-0) put their 38-game winning streak on the line once again Saturday as they host another of the 10 unbeaten teams left in D2, No. 9 Davenport, in a GLIAC showdown. While Ferris is favored any time it takes the field, the Bulldogs have won each of their last two games — against Michigan Tech and Grand Valley State — by just a touchdown after taking the two games before that by a combined score of 97-0. QB Wyatt Bower continues to lead the way with 1,243 passing yards and 537 more on the ground, with 19 total touchdowns. Davenport (8-0) has never beaten Ferris in 10 all-time meetings but is in the midst of the best season in the brief history of the program. That's due in large part to Harlon Hill Trophy candidate Cephus Harris, who is rushing for 198.4 yards per game and racked up 351 yards on the ground in the season opener against Gannon. He leads D2 with 1,587 yards and 21 touchdowns on the ground. Will the Bulldogs be able to keep him contained and stave off another upset bid? Here's all you need to know to watch. item.title: “We’re still working”: Eva Olid promises more from her free-flowing Man United Women team
item.description: “We’re still working”: Eva Olid promises more from her free-flowing Man United Women team Manchester United Women manager Eva Olid has spoken to the media ahead of her side’s match against Everton Women this afternoon. Evolution The first topic she addressed was how her team has evolved since the start of the season, explaining, “yeah, especially in terms of the confidence the team now have in possession and out of possession. We look like a totally different team, but, as I say, we’re still the same team. The only difference is that we’ve now had more weeks working together, and we can feel that we understand each other better.” She also stated that while her side can enjoy their current form, they must be prepared for changes, explaining, “we’re in a good moment, but we know how football works. During a season, you have ups and downs, and you always need to be ready for when things go well and when they don’t. You need to stay together and solve situations as a team. At the beginning of the season, we had two bad performances, but we were able to work together to understand what was happening and how we could improve.” The derby last weekend Reflecting on the 1-1 draw with Manchester City last weekend, Olid explained that the crowd numbers were similar to what she experienced in Heart of Midlothian matches against Hibernian, but overall, “we really enjoyed it. We were speaking with the staff about how much we enjoyed Sunday because the fans were with us. We could hear them, and these are the nights we are involved in football for. We enjoyed everything about it: the way the team played, the fans and the intensity of the game. These kinds of matches make us happy.” Spanish talent moving to club Olid was then asked about how she, her coaches, and player Andrea Medina are adapting to life at the club. She explained, “Spanish players and coaches are doing well here. Sometimes, especially for players, we say that they need a period of adaptation because the culture, the weather and everything else are different. But I think Andrea, for example, has adapted really well, and she’s very happy here.” Elaborating on what she loves about English football, she explained, “for me, the intensity of English football is really exciting. The players combine tactical awareness with technical ability, and that mix is exciting to watch. The physicality probably makes the game more intense, and combining that physicality with tactics and technical ability creates the perfect balance.” Olid also revealed that she was delighted that Elisabeth Terland scored on Sunday and that Ellen Wangerheim and Lea Schuller both got on the scoresheet on Wednesday night against Burnley in the cup. She also confirmed that everyone is available to play except Scarlett Hill. Featured image by Jess Hornby via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Manchester City vs Brighton: Latest team news, injury updates and predicted starting XI
item.description: Manchester City vs Brighton: Latest team news, injury updates and predicted starting XI Manchester City take on Brighton today at the Etihad Stadium in Premier League action. The two teams met on Wednesday night in the Carabao Cup. That game finished 2-2 with Enzo Maresca’s side claiming the fourth round tie 4-3 on penalties. Today’s match sees 1st vs 3rd on the Premier League table clash. It promises to be an entertaining match which should showcase what the Premier League is all about. Here is the latest Manchester City team news and injury updates, along with my predicted City starting eleven for today’s match. Latest City team and injury news. Manchester City only have one player unavailable for today’s match due to injury. Antoine Semenyo is ruled out of today’s game due to a knee injury. Matheus Nunes should return today as Enzo Maresca told the media yesterday that Semenyo is the only City player unavailable for today’s clash with Brighton. Erling Haaland, Josko Gvardiol, Elliot Anderson, Gianluigi Donnarumma, and Ruben Dias will all return for today’s game. All five players were rested for Manchester City’s midweek Carabao Cup tie against Fabian Hurzeler’s side. It would be a surprise if they all didn’t start in today’s game. In terms of team selection, it would be expected that Enzo Maresca will select his strongest available starting eleven today. In my opinion, Abdukodir Khusanov should start at centre-back alongside Ruben Dias. Matheus Nunes should slot in at right-back as City will need their pace against Brighton’s clever and quick front line. My predicted City starting eleven can be seen below. item.title: “It’s The Kobe Bryant Thing” – MLB Insider Reveals Behind-The-Scenes of Shohei Ohtani’s Controversial Decision During NLCS
item.description: Shohei Ohtani - LA Dodgers | © Imagn MLB insider Jim Bowden shared details about the Los Angeles Dodgers’ decision to keep Shohei Ohtani in the lineup despite fitness concerns during the 2026 National League Championship Series. Ohtani’s availability became a major talking point during the series against the Milwaukee Brewers. With the Dodgers trailing 0-3 and the Japanese superstar struggling at the plate, manager Dave Roberts, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, and general manager Brandon Gomes reportedly met with him ahead of Game 4. The Dodgers were concerned about Ohtani’s left knee irritation and right biceps tightness. The management considered removing him from the starting lineup to protect his health and give the offense a different look. However, Ohtani reportedly insisted on playing and refused to be benched for Game 4. While sharing these meeting details ahead of Game 4 on ‘97.1 The Fan LA,’ Bowden also said the Dodgers ultimately chose to trust their superstar rather than overrule his decision. “What the Dodgers chose to do was, I’m going to trust my superstar. He says he’s fine. And by the way, he homered in game four, right? So, I mean, we can’t really second guess that final decision when he sits there and homers that next game, right? But I think it’s the Kobe Bryant thing, right? Like with the Lakers, what would happen if Kobe went in and said, “I’m playing.” Kobe would have played, right? I know it’s a little different in the NBA. I get it. But I think what Dave Roberts and Andrew Friedman were doing was trusting their superstar. And I think we all understand that. And so they decided they were going to go with him.” However, Ohtani’s home run was not enough to prevent the Dodgers from being swept by Milwaukee. He hit a three-run homer in the second inning of Game 4 but struck out in his other three at-bats, including a crucial late-game appearance with the tying run at third base. He finished the 2026 postseason with a .192 batting average and 10 strikeouts. What did Shohei Ohtani say after the Dodgers’ postseason exit? After the Dodgers’ 6-4 defeat to the Brewers on October 15, Shohei Ohtani spoke to reporters in a post-game interview about the team’s elimination. He praised Milwaukee’s performance and acknowledged that the opponents had exposed weaknesses in his game. “The Brewers were overall strong, and a very good team. And [they] really exposed parts of me as a player, and got to give some credit to that,” said Shohei Ohtani. Shohei Ohtani’s injury concerns had also affected his availability during the regular season. He dealt with left knee inflammation in June and later missed time in September with right biceps inflammation. He finished the 2026 regular season with 523 at-bats, 89 runs, and 144 hits across 135 games. item.title: Emiliano Martinez reveals finger injury 'will NEVER return' to normal as Chelsea star admits to 'zombie' World Cup struggle with Argentina
item.description: Chelsea FC v Brighton & Hove Albion - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Emiliano Martinez has opened up on the harrowing physical toll of his career, admitting that a significant finger injury sustained earlier this year will never truly heal. The Chelsea goalkeeper revealed he was forced to play through extreme pain to help Argentina, leaving him with permanent damage that still affects his game today. Playing through the pain for Argentina Martinez suffered a broken and dislocated finger in May during the warm-up for Aston Villa's Europa League final victory against Freiburg. The severe injury immediately cast doubt over his involvement in Argentina's World Cup title defence, leaving the 34-year-old devastated when he first saw the scans. Rather than undergoing surgery that would have ruled him out of the tournament, Martinez chose to play through the agony. Backed by Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni, the shot-stopper relied on a customised Adidas glove for protection, despite admitting the heavy strapping severely restricted his ability to grasp the ball. 'Every single night I was crying' Speaking to Argentine journalist Gaston Edul’s YouTube channel, the veteran goalkeeper detailed the severe physical and emotional toll the injury took on his daily life. The pain was so intense that it completely altered his training methods and required immense personal sacrifice. "The day before Algeria I was diving with one arm, diving like a zombie," Martinez explained. "If I put my hand down I was seeing stars. It was brutal. Every single night I was crying because my finger looked like a sausage." Despite the permanent consequences, the Argentine insists he has no regrets about putting his country first. "It will never go back to how it was," he said. "I am still playing with pain. But these are the risks you take for the national team, I’d do it again." A collapsed transfer to Juventus The finger problem had significant ramifications for Martinez's club career during the summer window. A prospective move to Serie A giants Juventus ultimately broke down once the full extent of the damage was discovered during his medical assessments. "I got an x-ray and it was broken again," the goalkeeper revealed. "That is when a transfer to a club fell through because of the finger." Following the collapsed move to Italy, Martinez eventually secured a £7.5 million transfer to Chelsea. "They said it was possible for me to play like that, that I needed surgery, but Chelsea didn't, they didn't care," he added. "One day I will need surgery." Recovering from a broken jaw While his finger issue remains a long-term concern, Martinez is currently sidelined in west London with a completely different physical setback. The goalkeeper is actively recovering from a broken jaw sustained earlier this month during Chelsea's victory over Everton. He will now focus heavily on his rehabilitation before attempting to reclaim his spot in the starting XI at Stamford Bridge. Once

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro posts video, says he fled Brazil due to ‘persecution’
item.description: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro posted a video message on social media late Friday to declare he fled to the US because he was a victim of 'persecution'. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's election runoff to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, gave no details of how he left the country.

item.title: ‘Why I strangled, mutilated Adedotun Oluwaseun’ – Murder suspect who mourned with victim’s family
item.description: By Evelyn Usman For the family of Mrs Adedotun Oluwaseun, retirement was supposed to usher in a season of peace, rest and the joy of reaping the fruits of years of dedicated service. Instead, the death of their beloved mother has left them grieving and grappling with painful questions about the circumstances surrounding her final hours. Read Also: Police arrest suspect over murder of Adedotun Oluwaseun , retired Ogun teacher The retired confidential secretary with the Ogun State Universal Basic Education Board was allegedly strangled and repeatedly slashed with a machete in her residence at Bode Olude community, Abeokuta, Ogun State. A home that should have offered her security became the scene of a violent death, leaving her family searching for answers. Nearly eight months after the incident, the Ogun State Police Command announced a breakthrough with the arrest of 49-year-old Saburi Lateef, a popular transporter in Abeokuta, also known as Alhaji Oki Osan. In a disturbing twist, the suspect was reportedly among those who visited the deceased’s residence to commiserate with her family after her death, according to police sources. item.content:encoded: By Evelyn Usman For the family of Mrs Adedotun Oluwaseun, retirement was supposed to usher in a season of peace, rest and the joy of reaping the fruits of years of dedicated service. Instead, the death of their beloved mother has left them grieving and grappling with painful questions about the circumstances surrounding her final hours. Read Also: Police arrest suspect over murder of Adedotun Oluwaseun , retired Ogun teacher The retired confidential secretary with the Ogun State Universal Basic Education Board was allegedly strangled and repeatedly slashed with a machete in her residence at Bode Olude community, Abeokuta, Ogun State. A home that should have offered her security became the scene of a violent death, leaving her family searching for answers. Nearly eight months after the incident, the Ogun State Police Command announced a breakthrough with the arrest of 49-year-old Saburi Lateef, a popular transporter in Abeokuta, also known as Alhaji Oki Osan. In a disturbing twist, the suspect was reportedly among those who visited the deceased’s residence to commiserate with her family after her death, according to police sources. Investigation A source in the Homicide Section of the Ogun State Police Command, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said investigators initially had no clear lead to the perpetrator. According to the source: “At the beginning, there was no link to the perpetrator of the act, but the Commissioner of Police, CP Olubode Ojajuni, directed that we should ensure that we do everything possible to unravel the killers.” Police sources alleged that Lateef gained access to the deceased’s residence while she was away attending a retirement party organised for a friend around the Rounder area of Abeokuta. “He was ransacking the whole place when the woman returned. In his bid to prevent being exposed, he strangled the woman. “Not convinced that the woman was dead, he picked a cutlass and inflicted multiple cuts on her body. After that, he picked up her body and took it to the toilet, where he placed it on the closet to confirm if she was actually dead. “He spent more than an hour carrying out the act without attracting the attention of other residents in the neighbourhood,” the source alleged. ‘I don’t know what came over me’ — Suspect In his account, Lateef attributed his alleged action to frustration over the money he claimed Oluwaseun was keeping for him. He said: “I don’t know what came over me that day. She was owing me N3.45 million, being the proceeds of my truck, which I sold as scrap. I have known Big Mummy (the deceased) for about 10 years now. I knew her since when her building was under construction, but it was when she moved in that we became close. “It all started last year, when my truck broke down. I couldn’t get enough money to repair it. So, I parked it somewhere around my area in Bode Olude. After some time, some people came to buy it. “Before then, I had told Big Mummy (the deceased) that I needed a loan to buy another truck and she promised to give me. So, when I sold my truck, I handed over the remaining N3.45 million to her, just to let her know that I actually need the loan that she wanted to give me. “After some time, I asked her for the loan, which she had earlier promised me. She kept assuring me that she would give me at a later date, but she didn’t give me any loan. She kept extending the payment and I became very worried. “When the loan that she promised me was not forthcoming, I requested her to pay me my money, which I kept with her, but she again refused to give me my money,” he stated. Continuing his account, Lateef narrated how he allegedly gained entry into the deceased’s home and what happened when she returned. He said: “On that day, I was determined to collect my money. Though I was drunk, that was not the first time, nor the only time, that I had taken alcohol. I was just frustrated and I needed my money. “I gained access to her sitting room after I removed the burglary in one of the windows. When she came, we had a serious disagreement and I strangled her. After that, I picked a matchet in her apartment and inflicted cuts in different parts of her body,” he said. ‘We don’t know him’ — Bereaved family His account, however, was disputed by members of the deceased’s family, who insisted that they neither knew him as a friend of their mother nor had any knowledge of the alleged financial transaction. For the family, the arrest has raised fresh questions, particularly over Lateef’s claim that he had known the deceased for about a decade and had entrusted millions of naira to her. The deceased’s eldest daughter, Mrs Taiwo Atanda, described her mother’s death as a mystery, insisting that the family had never known Lateef to be associated with her. Recounting her last encounter with her mother, Atanda said: “On February 27, 2026, she came to my house when she was returning from her friend’s retirement party around Rounder area. She spent some hours with me and my children and, when it was getting dark, she went home. “Usually, she used to wake us every day to greet us and talk to my children. The following day, which was a Saturday, we didn’t hear anything from her. I asked my children and they said that she had not called. I thought her phone battery had gone flat,” she recounted. Worried by the unusual silence, Atanda said she contacted an elderly woman living close to her mother’s residence to find out whether she had seen her. “I called one Alhaja, who lives close to my mother, but she told me that she had not seen her for about two days. The Alhaja was at the mosque then because it was during Ramadan period. She promised to check on Big Mummy as soon as she finished from the mosque,” she said. According to Atanda, the woman later went to the deceased’s residence but found the surroundings dark, with no electricity. She reportedly proceeded to a nearby house where Oluwaseun usually visited, only to be told that she had not been seen for about three days. Atanda said the woman and the occupant of the nearby house subsequently went to her mother’s residence, where they discovered her body on the toilet closet, bearing multiple machete wounds. The discovery marked the beginning of an agonising search for answers for a family struggling to understand how their mother had died and what could have led to the killing. The circumstances surrounding the suspect’s reported presence among the mourners added another layer to their grief. Atanda said she was shocked to learn that Lateef had been among those who visited the house after her mother’s death. “We don’t know this man. We have been celebrating Christmas with my mother and we have never seen him in her house. My children used to spend their holidays in her house and nobody has ever seen him with her. The first time that I saw him was the following day after my mother was killed. He was one of the mourners that day,” she said. The daughter also denied that her mother had ever mentioned Lateef to the family or told them that she was keeping millions of naira for him. Family demands justice Atanda called on the Ogun State Government and the police to ensure that the circumstances surrounding her mother’s death were thoroughly investigated and that justice was served. For the family, the arrest of a suspect is only one part of the process. They want investigators to establish what happened inside Oluwaseun’s residence, examine the claims of a financial dispute and determine the circumstances that led to the killing. They insist that their mother’s death must not be left unresolved. Police assure of justice The Police Public Relations Officer of the Ogun State Police Command, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, attributed the breakthrough to the persistence, professionalism and commitment of officers and men of the command. He reiterated the command’s resolve to ensure that criminals had no hiding place in the state. Babaseyi

item.title: ‘I cry, break down behind closed doors’ – Funke Akindele reflects on pressures of being in the spotlight
item.description: By Aiyedun Oluwadamilola Nollywood actress and producer Funke Akindele has opened up about her emotional struggles behind the cameras, revealing that she sometimes cries and breaks down in private despite her cheerful public image. The actress made this known during an interview with CNN, where she reflected on the pressures of fame, public scrutiny of her relationships and the importance of prioritising personal well-being. “I cry. I lock myself in the room, cry, break down, and hit the bed. But I just pick myself up and come back to life,” Akindele said. The filmmaker, popularly associated with her ability to entertain audiences through her films and public appearances, acknowledged that the cheerful image people see does not always reflect what she experiences privately. She also spoke about the effect of public opinion on her personal life, recalling moments when she questioned her decisions and worried about how people would judge her. “Sometimes I tell myself, you’ve made a mistake again. How are people going to judge you?” she said, describing the thoughts she sometimes had to overcome. Akindele explained that she has gradually learnt to confront challenges and move forward rather than allow public opinion to determine how she sees herself. Beyond dealing with criticism, the actress highlighted the importance of self-care and maintaining relationships with loved ones while pursuing professional success. The post ‘I cry, break down behind closed doors’ – Funke Akindele reflects on pressures of being in the spotlight appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Taraba: Day bandits killed 62, injured 52, dislodged 7,123
item.description: • We can no longer farm, they took everything away from us — survivor By Femi Bolaji, Jalingo Friday, October 23, 2026, began like any other market day in Binnari, a rural community in Karim-Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State, where the life of the people revolves around farming, fishing, livestock rearing and cross border trade. Read Also: Death toll in Taraba bandits’ attack now 50 From the early hours, residents and traders from neighbouring communities were busy going about their daily activities. Farmers brought their produce to market, food sellers prepared for customers, and livestock owners hoped to make sales that would help sustain their families. For many, the market was more than a place to buy and sell. It was where household needs were met, school fees were raised, debts were settled and plans for the coming week were made. But before the day ended, that familiar routine had been violently interrupted. Armed bandits on motorbikes reportedly stormed the community, opening fire on people going about their business, killing residents, destroying property and looting stores. In the confusion that followed, families fled for safety, leaving behind homes, belongings and livelihoods they had spent years building. By the time the immediate danger had passed, Binnari had been left counting its losses. Casualties The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), in it’s preliminary reports from the Taraba State Emergency Management Agency (TSEMA) and posted on its official social media handles put the death toll at 62. Another 52 people were reported injured, while 5,187 residents were displaced and 7,123 people affected by the attack. The figures, contained in a statement issued by NEMA on October 27, 2026, followed an on-the-spot assessment by TSEMA’s Executive Secretary, Dr. Echuseh Audu. Behind those numbers are families struggling to understand how a day that began with ordinary hopes ended in death, displacement and uncertainty. For the people of Binnari, the tragedy is not simply about the number of lives lost. It is also about the children whose education may have been interrupted, the farmers who have lost their livestock, the traders who can no longer return to the market with confidence and the families now wondering how to begin again. In a community where people depend largely on what they produce, catch, rear or sell, the attack has threatened not only lives but the very means through which residents survive. Read Also: Death toll in Taraba bandits’ attack now 50 From the early hours, residents and traders from neighbouring communities were busy going about their daily activities. Farmers brought their produce to market, food sellers prepared for customers, and livestock owners hoped to make sales that would help sustain their families. For many, the market was more than a place to buy and sell. It was where household needs were met, school fees were raised, debts were settled and plans for the coming week were made. But before the day ended, that familiar routine had been violently interrupted. In the confusion that followed, families fled for safety, leaving behind homes, belongings and livelihoods they had spent years building. By the time the immediate danger had passed, Binnari had been left counting its losses. Casualties The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), in it’s preliminary reports from the Taraba State Emergency Management Agency (TSEMA) and posted on its official social media handles put the death toll at 62. Another 52 people were reported injured, while 5,187 residents were displaced and 7,123 people affected by the attack. The figures, contained in a statement issued by NEMA on October 27, 2026, followed an on-the-spot assessment by TSEMA’s Executive Secretary, Dr. Echuseh Audu. Behind those numbers are families struggling to understand how a day that began with ordinary hopes ended in death, displacement and uncertainty. For the people of Binnari, the tragedy is not simply about the number of lives lost. It is also about the children whose education may have been interrupted, the farmers who have lost their livestock, the traders who can no longer return to the market with confidence and the families now wondering how to begin again. In a community where people depend largely on what they produce, catch, rear or sell, the attack has threatened not only lives but the very means through which residents survive. Binnari’s market has long served as an important meeting point for people from different communities and neighbouring states like Plateau, Gombe and Bauchi. Farmers come with grain and other agricultural produce. Fishermen bring their catch, while livestock owners and traders gather to exchange goods and negotiate prices. For many residents, market day offers an opportunity to earn money, replenish household supplies and reconnect with people they may not have seen for days or weeks. Such exchanges have helped sustain families and strengthen relationships across community and state boundaries.That was the life Binnari’s residents knew before the attack. Attack On October 23, however, the market became the scene of a violent assault that residents say left people running for their lives.The attackers reportedly opened fire indiscriminately, killing people and destroying property. As fear spread, some residents fled towards nearby areas in search of safety. Others were caught in the confusion as people desperately tried to escape the violence. Accounts from the community also indicated that some people drowned after a canoe capsized during an attempt to cross a river while fleeing the attack. For those who survived, the experience was devastating. Some lost relatives, others lost their homes, and many were left without the means to provide food for their families. The fact that the attack happened on a market day made the tragedy particularly painful. People who had gathered to earn a living and attend to their daily needs suddenly found themselves fighting to stay alive. The preliminary figures released by NEMA offer an indication of the scale of the disaster, but they cannot fully capture the grief of families who lost loved ones or the anxiety of those who fled without knowing when they would return. For Ezekiel Salihu, a resident of Binnari, the attack has left the community in desperate need of government intervention. Recalling what happened, he said residents were engaged in their normal trading activities when the armed men arrived and began killing people and destroying property. “My name is Ezekiel Salihu. I am calling on the government,” he said in an emotional appeal. “We, the people of Binnari, are currently in a very difficult situation because of what happened recently. Bandits came into our town on Friday when everyone was buying and selling. People were going about their daily trading activities when the attackers came and started killing people and destroying properties.” Fear for future For Salihu, the immediate concern is whether residents can continue to live in their community without fear of another attack. He appealed to the government and security agencies in Karim-Lamido to deploy personnel to the area and provide the protection residents desperately need. “I am calling on the government and security agencies in Karim-Lamido to help us find a way to live peacefully in our town. Security forces should be deployed here so that we can feel safe,” he said. He also expressed concern about the closure of schools, saying the attack had disrupted the education of children in the community. “Our schools have all been closed down, and many students drowned and died as a result of the attack,” he added. Salihu’s appeal was directed particularly at Governor Agbu Kefas, whom he urged to act swiftly to prevent further suffering. “I am begging the government, especially Governor Kefas, to act swiftly and help us.” His concerns reflect the wider challenges facing Binnari. While the immediate priority is to prevent another attack, residents must also contend with disrupted education, lost income and the difficulty of restoring a sense of normal life. For parents, the fear is not limited to what has already happened. It is also about whether their children can safely return to school, whether family members can travel to nearby communities and whether farmers can return to their fields without risking their lives. For Maryam Abbas, the attack has taken away the means through which she supported herself and her family. A food seller, farmer and fisherwoman, Abbas depended on different sources of livelihood to meet household needs. Each activity played a role in helping her survive and provide for those who depended on her. But the attack left her facing an uncertain future. “My name is Maryam Abbas. I am a food seller, a farmer and a fisherwoman. On Friday, bandits came and attacked us. They burnt and destroyed our properties and killed many people. Our animals, including cows and goats, as well as other livestock, were stolen by the bandits,” she said. Her account reflects the experience of many rural households whose economic security depends on a combination of farming, trading, fishing and animal rearing. For such families, losing livestock is not simply losing animals. It can mean losing savings, trading capital and the resources needed to pay school fees, buy food or meet medical expenses. Similarly, when farm produce and equipment are destroyed, a family’s ability to earn money may be affected well beyond the day of the attack. Abbas said she and others had been left with virtually nothing and appealed to the government for assistance. “We have nothing left because we lost everything, but we are begging the government to help us. We want to live without the fear of being attacked,” she said. Her plea was particularly poignant because she did not see an easy al

item.title: 2027: Okorocha ‘never contested’ Imo West primary – Uzodimma’s aide
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA The Deputy Chief of Staff to Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, Chief Enyinna Onuegbu, has said former Governor Rochas Okorocha never took part in the All Progressives Congress APC primary for Imo West Senatorial District, which a Federal High Court in Abuja has now ruled he won. Read Also: Orlu Senatorial Seat: War in Imo as Okorocha battles Uzodimma Onuegbu, a lawyer, spoke on Friday evening on Arise News, monitored in Abuja, in a right of reply to Okorocha, who appeared on the same programme about 24 hours earlier. “Imo APC people never saw Okorocha as an aspirant and he didn’t participate and was not even physically present in Imo State anywhere at any level. Any briefing of stakeholders, any briefing of delegates, any event conducted prior to that primaries, Senator Okorocha was not physically present,” Onuegbu sai He asked at what stage Okorocha addressed party members as an aspirant. “At what stage did he consult? At what stage has he been able to provide evidence of I have been declared winner at any level, ward, LGA or state?” he asked. Onuegbu said the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the committee that conducted the primary both rejected the documents Okorocha relied on before the court. “When the court, in its own documentation, the processes filed in court, showed that both INEC, the authority that supervised, APC committee that conducted, all denied the documents His Excellency Rochas Okorocha relied on. Before the court, they all denied them as forgeries, fictitious, and totally fabricated,” he said. According to him, the court “chose to rely on what applicant filed without averting its mind to the need to resolve the conflict in the documentation brought by both parties.” Onuegbu argued that where documents conflict in an originating summons, “the law requires the court to resolve the conflict by oral evidence of witnesses.” In his words, “What the law requires the court to do is to call evidence of witnesses so that they can be put to cross-examination.” He added that the Supreme Court had held that “when forgeries are alleged, what the court is left to do is to put the parties to the witness box.” Asked whether Uzodimma’s side had been denied the chance to present its own documents, Onuegbu said that was not the point. “He put forward documents and we put documents that showed that the authority that did the work disputed what he put. He was an aspirant like he was. Governor Hope Uzodimma was not the person who declared the result,” he said. item.content:encoded: By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA The Deputy Chief of Staff to Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, Chief Enyinna Onuegbu, has said former Governor Rochas Okorocha never took part in the All Progressives Congress APC primary for Imo West Senatorial District, which a Federal High Court in Abuja has now ruled he won. Read Also: Orlu Senatorial Seat: War in Imo as Okorocha battles Uzodimma Onuegbu, a lawyer, spoke on Friday evening on Arise News, monitored in Abuja, in a right of reply to Okorocha, who appeared on the same programme about 24 hours earlier. “Imo APC people never saw Okorocha as an aspirant and he didn’t participate and was not even physically present in Imo State anywhere at any level. Any briefing of stakeholders, any briefing of delegates, any event conducted prior to that primaries, Senator Okorocha was not physically present,” Onuegbu sai He asked at what stage Okorocha addressed party members as an aspirant. “At what stage did he consult? At what stage has he been able to provide evidence of I have been declared winner at any level, ward, LGA or state?” he asked. Onuegbu said the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the committee that conducted the primary both rejected the documents Okorocha relied on before the court. “When the court, in its own documentation, the processes filed in court, showed that both INEC, the authority that supervised, APC committee that conducted, all denied the documents His Excellency Rochas Okorocha relied on. Before the court, they all denied them as forgeries, fictitious, and totally fabricated,” he said. According to him, the court “chose to rely on what applicant filed without averting its mind to the need to resolve the conflict in the documentation brought by both parties.” Onuegbu argued that where documents conflict in an originating summons, “the law requires the court to resolve the conflict by oral evidence of witnesses.” In his words, “What the law requires the court to do is to call evidence of witnesses so that they can be put to cross-examination.” He added that the Supreme Court had held that “when forgeries are alleged, what the court is left to do is to put the parties to the witness box.” Asked whether Uzodimma’s side had been denied the chance to present its own documents, Onuegbu said that was not the point. “He put forward documents and we put documents that showed that the authority that did the work disputed what he put. So this contradiction can only be resolved” by hearing witnesses, he said. He rejected Okorocha’s reference to “Hope’s document,” saying the governor did not run the exercise. “Governor Hope Uzodimma was not the one who conducted the primaries. He was an aspirant like he was. Governor Hope Uzodimma was not the person who declared the result,” he said. On the time Okorocha took to go to court, Onuegbu cited the Electoral Act. “When you tell me that the Electoral Act says any challenge to the result of a primary must be filed within 14 days, and you’re telling me a person who filed 87 days was right because that is when he became aware, it means that he was not aware of his victory too, which he claims,” he said. He also questioned why Okorocha had shown no sign of having won. “A person who participated in an election in his senatorial district did not call for celebration in his community, his family, did not celebrate his victory, does not have a video recording, pictures of where he celebrated his victory or where his hand was raised up, something is wrong somewhere,” he said. “When you tell me that a man who won did not come to party office to say, party people, thank you for electing me, a former governor of the state, something is wrong somewhere,” he added. Onuegbu said Okorocha bypassed the party’s own complaint channels. “If you were in any manner denied your victory, the guidelines of the party provide for the steps you would take. There is a panel that goes into complaints after primary election results. There is an Appeal Committee that supervises the conduct of the first panel. “Did he exhaust those domestic avenues set up in the guidelines of party primaries of the All Progressives Congress? The answer is no. He sat by in Abuja, concocted his documents and waited for when he would file at his chosen forum,” he said. He also dismissed the affidavit filed on Okorocha’s behalf by his son. “His son, biological son, who is unfortunately being dragged into this, is not an APC member, did not participate in any of the processes and cannot depose to an affidavit in support of facts for which they have gotten a judgment that apparently will be challenged on appeal,” he said. Pressed on whether his camp accepted that the court had spoken, Onuegbu said the court of first instance was only “the first rung of the ladder.” “The court has spoken and we are contesting that what the court said is illegal, is not based on law, is not based on the facts of the matter. If we accept, we wouldn’t be on appeal. As far as we are concerned, this matter of what the judgment is, is for the Appeal Court. “We have seen the capacity of the court from the judgment now. The knowledge of the court is now before the public and will be tested on appeal,” he added. item.title: Orlu Senatorial Seat: War in Imo as Okorocha battles Uzodimma
item.description: •Court grants Okorocha ticket, 12 Chairmen back go vernor By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA The fight over who flies the All Progressives Congress (APC) flag in Imo West Senatorial District has turned into open war, with the party’s 12 local government chairmen in the zone rejecting a court judgment that handed the ticket to former Governor Rochas Okorocha and insisting that Governor Hope Uzodimma remains the candidate. Read Also: Tinubu has broken Imo’s shackles — Okorocha hails court judgment The chairmen made their stand known on Friday at a press conference in Owerri, a day after a Federal High Court in Abuja sacked Uzodimma as the party’s candidate for the January 16, 2027 Senate election. State APC chairman, Austin Onyedebelu spoke on behalf of the Chairmen. Said he: “We reject this judgment in its entirety because it is an undisguised travesty of justice. It is a political robbery clothed in legal robes, the latest instalment of a satanic scheme hatched by Abuja politicians against the South-East,” the chairmen declared. Justice Obiora Egwuatu ruled on Thursday that Okorocha, and not the governor, won the party’s May 18 primary for the district. He held that Okorocha had produced “sufficient evidence” that he won the exercise, which was monitored by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Court order The court ordered the APC to forward Okorocha’s name to INEC and directed the commission to publish him as the party’s validly nominated candidate. It also barred Uzodimma from presenting himself as the APC candidate in the election.
